/** Estimated tokens of what would actually be sent (markers included). */

export function viewTokenEstimate(nodes: ViewNode[]): number {

let total = 0;

for (const n of nodes) {

if (n.deleted) continue;

total += estimateTokens(n.content) + estimateTokens(marker(n.msg.seq)) + 4;

// flat per-attachment estimate, matching what turn.ts bills at append time

if (n.msg.media) total += 1500;

if (n.msg.role === "assistant" && n.msg.tool_calls) {

for (const c of parseToolCalls(n.msg)) total += estimateTokens(c.arguments);

}

}

return total;

}

 

export function sessionViewEstimate(sessionId: string): number {

return viewTokenEstimate(projectView(sessionId));

}

import { lookupModel, type ModelInfo } from "../providers/models.ts";

import { lastPromptTokens } from "../store/db.ts";

 

export function modelBudget(model: string): ModelInfo {

return lookupModel(model);

}

 

/**

* Absolute prompt-token ceiling for auto-compaction (0 = window fraction only).

*

* The window fraction alone is exactly as trustworthy as lookupModel's idea of

* the window, and that number is best-effort: the endpoint's own /models

* listing often omits a context field, and the models.dev catalog then answers

* with a size the endpoint does not actually serve — 1,048,576 for

* glm-5.3-flash, 100,000,000 for one local proxy. Against such a window

* 0.85 * window is unreachable, so compaction never fired and the context

* grew monotonically to the provider's real limit, re-billed in full on every

* step. This ceiling is the quota-side guard that holds regardless of whether

* the window is right.

*/

export const DEFAULTCOMPACTATTOKENS = 131072;

 

/**

* Prompt tokens at which compaction fires: the smaller of the window fraction

* and the absolute ceiling. Shared by checkBudget (what tells the agent to

* prune) and compactIfNeeded (what actually fires) so the nudge and the thing

* it describes cannot drift apart.

*/

export function triggerTokens(model: string, compactAt = 0.85, compactAtTokens = DEFAULTCOMPACTAT_TOKENS): number {

const windowAt = Math.floor(modelBudget(model).contextWindow * compactAt);

return compactAtTokens > 0 ? Math.min(windowAt, compactAtTokens) : windowAt;

}

 

export interface BudgetCheck {

/** provider-reported size of the last request's prompt; 0 before the first call */

reported: number;

limit: number;

over: boolean;

ratio: number;

}

 

/**

* How full the context window is, per the provider's own accounting.

*

* This deliberately does not estimate: lastPromptTokens is the number the

* API billed us for the previous call, which includes the system prompt, tool

* schemas and message framing — everything a chars/4 estimate had to fudge

* (PROMPTOVERHEADTOKENS, RIP). Before the first call there is no report and

* the window is definitionally near-empty, so reported is 0 and over false.

*

* over is measured against triggerTokens, not the raw fraction — the agent

* must be told when the compaction threshold is near, which on an overstated

* window is far below the fraction of the window the same report is divided by.

*/

export function checkBudget(

sessionId: string,

model: string,

_unused = 0,

compactAt = 0.85,

compactAtTokens = DEFAULTCOMPACTAT_TOKENS,

): BudgetCheck {

const info = modelBudget(model);

const reported = lastPromptTokens(sessionId);

return {

reported,

limit: info.contextWindow,

over: reported >= triggerTokens(model, compactAt, compactAtTokens),

ratio: reported / info.contextWindow,

};

}

52:export async function compactIfNeeded(

// Host-driven auto-compaction. When the last provider-reported prompt size

// reaches the compaction trigger (see budget.ts), the oldest span — everything

// above a protected tail of the newest KEEP_TOKENS — is summarized by the model

// itself and hidden with a single delete+summary op — the same machinery

// ctx uses, so /undo reverts it too.

import { appendOps, lastPromptTokens } from "../store/db.ts";

import type { ChatMessage, ChatFn } from "../providers/types.ts";

import { estimateTokens } from "../providers/models.ts";

import { projectView, visibleNodes } from "./view.ts";

import { viewTokenEstimate } from "./render.ts";

import { DEFAULTCOMPACTAT_TOKENS, triggerTokens } from "./budget.ts";

import type { AgentEvent } from "../core/events.ts";

 

/**

* Newest history a compaction leaves visible, in tokens.

*

* This used to be a fraction of the window (55% of it, plus a 35% tail that was

* never compactable at all), which on a window the registry overstates means

* "keep half a million tokens". A keep-size is the only form that is correct

* no matter what the window turns out to be — and it is what every other harness

* does (opencode keeps 15_000). Bounded by half the trigger below, so a

* compaction always frees something.

*/

const KEEPTOKENS = 32000;

 

function summarizePrompt(): ChatMessage[] {

return [

{

role: "user",

content:

"Summarize this transcript segment for a coding agent that will continue working without it. " +

"Keep: goals, decisions made, files touched (paths), commands run and their outcomes, current state, next steps. " +

"Drop: raw tool output, false starts, boilerplate. Max ~300 words, terse bullet style. Output only the summary.",

},

];

}

 

async function llmSummary(chat: ChatFn, cfg: Parameters<ChatFn>[0], segment: string, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<string> {

let text = "";

const messages: ChatMessage[] = [...summarizePrompt(), { role: "user", content: segment }];

for await (const ev of chat(cfg, messages, [], signal)) {

if (ev.type === "text") text += ev.delta;

else if (ev.type === "done" && ev.reason.startsWith("error")) break;

}

return text.trim();

}

 

/**

* Check the budget and, if needed, hide the oldest span behind a summary.

* Returns a compacted event when compaction happened, null otherwise.

*/

export async function compactIfNeeded(

sessionId: string,

cfg: Parameters<ChatFn>[0],

chat: ChatFn,

opts: { compactAt?: number; compactAtTokens?: number; signal?: AbortSignal } = {},

): Promise<AgentEvent | null> {

/**

* The trigger is the provider's own last-reported prompt size — the one

* number that is definitionally the truth about how full the window is. A

* chars/4 estimate used to drive this, which both over-fired on dense

* Unicode and under-fired on chatty English. No report yet means no

* completed call yet, which means the window cannot be full.

*

* triggerTokens additionally caps the report against an absolute number,

* because the window it would be measured against is a best-effort guess

* (see DEFAULTCOMPACTAT_TOKENS): a report below 0.85 * window is not

* evidence that the window is really that large.

*/

const trigger = triggerTokens(cfg.model, opts.compactAt ?? 0.85, opts.compactAtTokens ?? DEFAULTCOMPACTAT_TOKENS);

const reported = lastPromptTokens(sessionId);

if (!reported || reported < trigger) return null;

const before = reported;

// half the trigger at most: a compaction that frees nothing is a billable

// summarization call that leaves the next step just as expensive

const keep = Math.min(KEEP_TOKENS, Math.floor(trigger / 2));

 

const nodes = projectView(sessionId);

 

// pick oldest-span candidates up to the protected tail boundary

const vis = visibleNodes(nodes);

// the newest keep tokens are never compacted; the 6-node floor keeps very

// short sessions coherent

let tail = Math.min(vis.length, 6);

let tailTok = 0;

for (let i = vis.length - 1; i >= 0 && tailTok < keep; i--) {

tailTok += estimateTokens(vis[i].content) + 8;

tail = Math.max(tail, vis.length - i);

}

const maxBoundary = vis.length - tail;

if (maxBoundary <= 1) return null;

 

const protectFrom = before - keep;

// Per-node numbers below ARE chars/4 estimates — but they only decide where

// to cut, never whether to cut, so an inaccurate node size costs a

// slightly different boundary, not a wrong compaction.

let acc = 0;

let boundary = 0; // exclusive index into vis

for (; boundary < maxBoundary; boundary++) {

acc += estimateTokens(vis[boundary].content) + 8;

if (acc >= protectFrom) break;

}

if (boundary <= 0) return null;

const candidates = vis.slice(0, boundary).filter((n) => n.msg.role !== "user" || n.content.length > 0);

 

const segment = candidates

.map((n) => [${n.msg.seq}] ${n.msg.role}: ${n.content.slice(0, 2000)})

.join("\n\n")

.slice(-120_000); // cap the summarizer input itself

 

let summary = "";

try {

summary = await llmSummary(chat, cfg, segment, opts.signal);

} catch {

summary = ""; // fall through to mechanical note

}

if (!summary) summary = (auto-compacted ${candidates.length} older messages to free context; originals in storage);

 

const ids = candidates.map((n) => n.msg.seq);

appendOps(sessionId, [{ kind: "delete", ids, summary }]);

 

const after = viewTokenEstimate(projectView(sessionId)) + 1500;

return { type: "compacted", removed: ids, tokensbefore: before, tokensafter: after };

}

The user asked me to help fix the token count bug in fox-agent. I've been investigating. Let me now formulate the actual fix and implement it.

 

Root cause: fox-agent's budget/compaction trigger relies on lastPromptTokens — the provider-reported prompt size. But on the kimi openai-compatible endpoint, that number was garbage (76319 with cached==prompt, while actual request was ~2.1M tokens). Result: compaction never fired, status bar showed 7%, and the request eventually blew the 1M limit → HTTP 400.

 

Fix approach: cross-check the provider report against a local estimate of the actual rendered context. If viewTokenEstimate(messages) (which is what would actually be sent) is much larger than the reported number, trust the estimate — compact early. Concretely:

 

1. In compactIfNeeded / checkBudget: use effectivePromptSize = max(reported, viewTokenEstimate) or trigger when the local estimate of the rendered messages exceeds the trigger. Actually a cleaner fix: compact when EITHER the report OR the local estimate of rendered messages exceeds the trigger. The estimate is chars/4 which underestimates for code/JSON... but for a 2M-char history it would still be ~500k chars/4... wait the DB said SUM(tokens)=1.96M for 10222 messages, and requested was 2.1M. estimateTokens is chars/4 — the stored tokens column. SUM(tokens) ≈ 1.96M vs requested 2.1M — actually the estimate was pretty accurate! So sessionViewEstimate would have flagged ~2M tokens well above the 131k trigger, and compaction would have fired.

 

So the fix: in checkBudget and compactIfNeeded, use max(provider-reported, local estimate of visible view). That keeps provider truth when sane, but catches garbage reports.

 

Also fix the status bar to show the same combined number (app.ts line 3207).

* triggerTokens additionally caps the report against an absolute number,

* because the window it would be measured against is a best-effort guess

* (see DEFAULTCOMPACTAT_TOKENS): a report below 0.85 * window is not

* evidence that the window is really that large.

const trigger = triggerTokens(cfg.model, opts.compactAt ?? 0.85, opts.compactAtTokens ?? DEFAULTCOMPACTAT_TOKENS);

const reported = lastPromptTokens(sessionId);

if (!reported || reported < trigger) return null;

const before = reported;

// half the trigger at most: a compaction that frees nothing is a billable

// summarization call that leaves the next step just as expensive

const keep = Math.min(KEEP_TOKENS, Math.floor(trigger / 2));

 

const nodes = projectView(sessionId);

 

// pick oldest-span candidates up to the protected tail boundary

const vis = visibleNodes(nodes);

// the newest keep tokens are never compacted; the 6-node floor keeps very

// short sessions coherent

let tail = Math.min(vis.length, 6);

let tailTok = 0;

for (let i = vis.length - 1; i >= 0 && tailTok < keep; i--) {

tailTok += estimateTokens(vis[i].content) + 8;

tail = Math.max(tail, vis.length - i);

}

const maxBoundary = vis.length - tail;

if (maxBoundary <= 1) return null;

 

const protectFrom = before - keep;

// Per-node numbers below ARE chars/4 estimates — but they only decide where

// to cut, never whether to cut, so an inaccurate node size costs a

// slightly different boundary, not a wrong compaction.

let acc = 0;

let boundary = 0; // exclusive index into vis

for (; boundary < maxBoundary; boundary++) {

acc += estimateTokens(vis[boundary].content) + 8;

if (acc >= protectFrom) break;

}

if (boundary <= 0) return null;

const candidates = vis.slice(0, boundary).filter((n) => n.msg.role !== "user" || n.content.length > 0);

.map((n) => [${n.msg.seq}] ${n.msg.role}: ${n.content.slice(0, 2000)})

.join("\n\n")

.slice(-120_000); // cap the summarizer input itself

summary = await llmSummary(chat, cfg, segment, opts.signal);

} catch {

summary = ""; // fall through to mechanical note

}

if (!summary) summary = (auto-compacted ${candidates.length} older messages to free context; originals in storage);

 

const ids = candidates.map((n) => n.msg.seq);

appendOps(sessionId, [{ kind: "delete", ids, summary }]);

 

const after = viewTokenEstimate(projectView(sessionId)) + 1500;

return { type: "compacted", removed: ids, tokensbefore: before, tokensafter: after };

}

import { lookupModel, type ModelInfo } from "../providers/models.ts";

import { lastPromptTokens } from "../store/db.ts";

 

export function modelBudget(model: string): ModelInfo {

return lookupModel(model);

}

 

/**

* Absolute prompt-token ceiling for auto-compaction (0 = window fraction only).

*

* The window fraction alone is exactly as trustworthy as lookupModel's idea of

* the window, and that number is best-effort: the endpoint's own /models

* listing often omits a context field, and the models.dev catalog then answers

* with a size the endpoint does not actually serve — 1,048,576 for

* glm-5.3-flash, 100,000,000 for one local proxy. Against such a window

* 0.85 * window is unreachable, so compaction never fired and the context

* grew monotonically to the provider's real limit, re-billed in full on every

* step. This ceiling is the quota-side guard that holds regardless of whether

* the window is right.

*/

export const DEFAULTCOMPACTATTOKENS = 131072;

 

/**

* Prompt tokens at which compaction fires: the smaller of the window fraction

* and the absolute ceiling. Shared by checkBudget (what tells the agent to

* prune) and compactIfNeeded (what actually fires) so the nudge and the thing

* it describes cannot drift apart.

*/

export function triggerTokens(model: string, compactAt = 0.85, compactAtTokens = DEFAULTCOMPACTAT_TOKENS): number {

const windowAt = Math.floor(modelBudget(model).contextWindow * compactAt);

return compactAtTokens > 0 ? Math.min(windowAt, compactAtTokens) : windowAt;

}

 

export interface BudgetCheck {

/** provider-reported size of the last request's prompt; 0 before the first call */

reported: number;

limit: number;

over: boolean;

ratio: number;

}

 

/**

* How full the context window is, per the provider's own accounting.

*

* This deliberately does not estimate: lastPromptTokens is the number the

* API billed us for the previous call, which includes the system prompt, tool

* schemas and message framing — everything a chars/4 estimate had to fudge

* (PROMPTOVERHEADTOKENS, RIP). Before the first call there is no report and

* the window is definitionally near-empty, so reported is 0 and over false.

*

* over is measured against triggerTokens, not the raw fraction — the agent

* must be told when the compaction threshold is near, which on an overstated

* window is far below the fraction of the window the same report is divided by.

*/

export function checkBudget(

sessionId: string,

model: string,

_unused = 0,

compactAt = 0.85,

compactAtTokens = DEFAULTCOMPACTAT_TOKENS,

): BudgetCheck {

const info = modelBudget(model);

const reported = lastPromptTokens(sessionId);

return {

reported,

limit: info.contextWindow,

over: reported >= triggerTokens(model, compactAt, compactAtTokens),

ratio: reported / info.contextWindow,

};

}

[145]agent

Why it happened

 

The short version: fox-agent trusted a broken token number from the provider, so it never realized the context was full.

 

The chain

 

1. Compaction is gated on the provider's report, and nothing else. compactIfNeeded() (src/context/compact.ts) decides whether to compact by reading lastPromptTokens(sessionId) — the prompt-token count from the last API response — and comparing it to a trigger threshold. Same number drives the "ctx N%" status bar and the checkBudget() nudge.

 

2. Your provider (kimi-code-plan-cn, openai-compatible) reports a bogus count. I pulled the usage table from the dead session (mv0ucgs0cd9d3caa.db). The final requests, seconds before the HTTP 400 ("requested: 2099907"), were recorded as:

 

```

prompttokens=76319 cachedtokens=76319 completion_tokens=159

```

 

The real request was ~2.1M tokens. So the provider was reporting something ~28x smaller than reality (most likely only uncached input tokens — note cached == prompt, meaning "all of it was a cache read, so you weren't billed for it" — but that's a billing figure, not a window-size figure).

 

3. The report said "7% full," so compaction never fired. With the report pinned at ~76k against a 1,048,576 window, reported < trigger was always true. The "Metadata acknowledged — context at 7%" line the stuck session kept repeating was it parroting this wrong number back. Context grew monotonically — 1.96M tokens of SUM(tokens) across 10,219 messages — until the provider itself rejected the request at 2,099,907.

 

4. fox-agent had no second opinion. The one guard that could have caught this — DEFAULT_COMPACT_AT_TOKENS = 131_072 — is an absolute ceiling on the trigger, so it only helps when the report is too big. There was no floor: nothing cross-checked the report against the locally-estimated size of the visible history, which for that session was ~520k tokens (chars/4). A report of 76k claiming to represent a 520k-token history is obviously wrong, but nothing in the code noticed.

 

The fix I was applying (3 files)

 

Add that missing cross-check: effectivePromptTokens(sessionId) in budget.ts returns the provider report, unless it's more than 2x the local estimate (chars/4 over visible messages) — in which case the estimate is used instead, since the estimate is a floor the real prompt can't be under. Wire it into:

 

• compactIfNeeded trigger (so compaction fires even when the provider under-reports)

• checkBudget (so the agent gets the nudge)

• the TUI status bar (so "ctx %" stops lying)

 

This session's own metadata shows the same live bug: "Context used: 54973/1048576 (5%), provider-reported" — the same misleading reading that killed the other session.

 

Want me to finish verifying the fix (typecheck + compact tests), or would you rather review the diff first?

export * as SessionUsage from "./usage.js"

 

import type { Usage } from "@opencode/ai"

import { Money } from "@opencode/schema/money"

import type { TokenUsage } from "@opencode/schema/token-usage"

import type { Model } from "@opencode/schema/model"

 

const finite = (value: number) => (Number.isFinite(value) ? value : 0)

const safe = (value: number | undefined) => Math.max(0, finite(value ?? 0))

 

export const tokens = (usage: Usage | undefined): TokenUsage.Info => ({

input: safe(usage?.nonCachedInputTokens),

output: safe(usage?.visibleOutputTokens),

reasoning: safe(usage?.reasoningTokens),

cache: {

read: safe(usage?.cacheReadInputTokens),

write: safe(usage?.cacheWriteInputTokens),

},

})

 

// TODO(#35765): Use Copilot's reported billed amount once billing has a dedicated typed runtime contract.

export function calculateCost(costs: Model.Info["cost"], usage: TokenUsage.Info) {

const context = usage.input + usage.cache.read + usage.cache.write

const tier = costs

.filter((cost) => cost.tier?.type === "context" && context > cost.tier.size)

.toSorted((a, b) => (b.tier?.size ?? 0) - (a.tier?.size ?? 0))[0]

const cost = tier ?? costs.find((cost) => cost.tier === undefined)

if (!cost) return Money.USD.zero

return Money.USD.make(

(usage.input * finite(cost.input) +

(usage.output + usage.reasoning) * finite(cost.output) +

usage.cache.read * finite(cost.cache.read) +

usage.cache.write * finite(cost.cache.write)) /

1000000,

)

}

 

export type Recorded = { readonly tokens: TokenUsage.Info; readonly cost: Money.USD }

 

export const record = (usage: Usage | undefined, costs: Model.Info["cost"]): Recorded => {

const normalized = tokens(usage)

return { tokens: normalized, cost: calculateCost(costs, normalized) }

}

 

export const add = (a: Recorded, b: Recorded): Recorded => ({

cost: Money.USD.make(a.cost + b.cost),

tokens: {

input: a.tokens.input + b.tokens.input,

output: a.tokens.output + b.tokens.output,

reasoning: a.tokens.reasoning + b.tokens.reasoning,

cache: {

read: a.tokens.cache.read + b.tokens.cache.read,

write: a.tokens.cache.write + b.tokens.cache.write,

},

},

})

measured: 0,

The smoking gun is confirmed — that harness line itself shows the bug: "Context used at your last step: 63550/1048576 tokens (6%), provider-reported" — but the dead session proved the real on-the-wire request was ~2.1M tokens at 6% by the same metric.

 

Provider verification (the root cause)

 

Direct probe of your provider (kimi-for-coding @ api.kimi.com/coding/v1):

 

│ "usage": {

│ "prompt_tokens": 88, "completion_tokens": 10, "total_tokens": 98,

│ "cached_tokens": 88,

│ "prompt_tokens_details": { "cached_tokens": 88 }

│ }

 

*prompt_tokens counts only new/uncached* input.** All 88 input tokens were cache reads (cached_tokens: 88), so it reported prompt_tokens: 88. On a fully cache-hit turn the provider reports a tiny number regardless of the megabytes of history actually transmitted. That's the whole bug: fox-agent stores prompt_tokens (76k) as "the prompt size," the trigger never fires, and the real 2.1M-token request eventually hits the provider's hard 1M limit → HTTP 400.

 

Note the endpoint does expose the truth — prompt_tokens + prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens = total input on the wire (88+88=176... well, total_tokens = prompt+billed completion; the full input is prompt_tokens + cached_tokens).

 

How opencode-v2 handles context size

 

opencode-v2 does not trust prompt_tokens alone. From packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts (estimatePrompt):

 

│ // The prompt size: `measured` is what the provider reported at the latest

│ // response, `estimated` is the text since.

│ return {

│ measured: tokens.input + tokens.cache.read + tokens.cache.write

│ + tokens.output + tokens.reasoning,

│ estimated: unmeasured.reduce((sum, m) => sum + estimateMessage(m), 0),

│ }

 

Three things fox-agent doesn't do:

 

1. Counts cached tokens as real context. tokens.input there is non-cached input (their SessionUsage.tokens maps input = nonCachedInputTokens), and they explicitly add cache.read + cache.write back in. Cache reads still occupy the context window. fox-agent throws cached_tokens away for budgeting.

2. Anchors the measurement to a message and estimates the delta since. They find the last assistant message with recorded usage ("anchor"), take its measured total, then Token.estimate (chars/4, in util/token.ts) every message added since. Measured + estimated = current context. fox-agent uses only the last report, which silently excludes anything appended after it.

3. Fits maxTokens to the remaining room. outputLimit() computes room = context - measured - estimated*(1+ESTIMATE_ERROR) and clamps the response budget so prompt+output stay inside the window — a second guard that prevents the oversized request from ever being built.

 

Summary

 

│ │ fox-agent │ opencode-v2 │

├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┤

│ What it trusts │ prompt_tokens (uncached │ non-cached + cache.read + │

│ │ only) │ cache.write │

│ Cache reads counted as │ No │ Yes │

│ context? │ │ │

│ History appended after last │ Ignored │ Chars/4-estimated and added │

│ report │ │ │

│ Output budget │ Fixed │ Clamped to remaining window │

 

The minimal correct fix for fox-agent: when recording usage, store prompt_tokens + cached_tokens as the effective prompt size (or sum them at read time in lastPromptTokens). Want me to implement that, plus the estimate-the-delta-since-anchor piece?

* cachedTokens is input read from the prefix cache — a subset of

* promptTokens, not a third bucket, so the index row's running totals still

* add up to what was billed. Optional because it is genuinely optional

* information: a call site (or a test) with nothing to report means "no cache

* detail", which is 0.

*/

export function recordUsage(

sessionId: string,

messageId: string | null,

promptTokens: number,

completionTokens: number,

cachedTokens = 0,

) {

// explicit columns: a migrated session has cached_tokens appended AFTER

// created_at, so a positional VALUES would put the timestamp in it

sessionDb(sessionId)

.prepare("INSERT INTO usage (sessionid, messageid, prompttokens, completiontokens, cachedtokens, createdat) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)")

.run(sessionId, messageId, promptTokens, completionTokens, cachedTokens, Date.now());

// running totals on the index row too, so a session listing never has to open

// the file to answer "how much has this session burned" — NULL means a legacy

// row awaiting backfill, which COALESCE treats as zero going forward

indexDb()

.prepare(

"UPDATE sessions SET prompttokens = COALESCE(prompttokens, 0) + ?, completiontokens = COALESCE(completiontokens, 0) + ?, cachedtokens = COALESCE(cachedtokens, 0) + ? WHERE id = ?",

)

.run(promptTokens, completionTokens, cachedTokens, sessionId);

}

 

/** Backfill the index's token totals from the session file (legacy rows). */

export function backfillUsage(sessionId: string): { prompt: number; completion: number; cached: number } {

const u = sessionUsage(sessionId);

indexDb()

.prepare("UPDATE sessions SET prompttokens = ?, completiontokens = ?, cached_tokens = ? WHERE id = ?")

.run(u.prompt, u.completion, u.cached, sessionId);

return u;

}

 

/**

* Legacy-row repair for preview: read the last user/assistant text message

* from the session's own database once and cache it in the index. An empty

* result is cached as "" so the listing doesn't reopen the file forever.

*/

export function backfillPreview(sessionId: string): string {

const m = sessionDb(sessionId)

.prepare("SELECT content FROM messages WHERE session_id = ? AND role IN ('user', 'assistant') AND content != '' ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1")

.get(sessionId) as { content: string } | null;

const preview = m ? m.content.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim().slice(0, 120) : "";

indexDb().prepare("UPDATE sessions SET preview = ? WHERE id = ?").run(preview, sessionId);

return preview;

}

 

/**

* A session's billing from its own file: the input that was re-sent from the

* prefix cache is summed alongside what was billed, so a hit rate is

* cached / prompt without a second query.

*/

export function sessionUsage(sessionId: string): { prompt: number; completion: number; cached: number } {

const r = sessionDb(sessionId)

.query(

"SELECT COALESCE(SUM(prompttokens),0) AS p, COALESCE(SUM(completiontokens),0) AS c, COALESCE(SUM(cachedtokens),0) AS k FROM usage WHERE sessionid = ?",

)

.get(sessionId) as { p: number; c: number; k: number };

return { prompt: r.p, completion: r.c, cached: r.k };

}

 

/**

* Most recent provider-reported prompt size — i.e. how big the context

* actually was last call. Unlike sessionUsage().prompt (a running total) this

* tracks the live window and drops after a compaction.

*/

export function lastPromptTokens(sessionId: string): number {

const r = sessionDb(sessionId)

.query("SELECT prompttokens AS p FROM usage WHERE sessionid = ? ORDER BY created_at DESC, rowid DESC LIMIT 1")

.get(sessionId) as { p: number } | undefined;

return r?.p ?? 0;

}

* Parsed msg.tool_calls, memoized on the immutable row. The render path used

* to JSON.parse every assistant node's call list on every step of every turn —

* the single most repeated parse in the loop. Message rows never change once

* written, so the raw string is the cache key's version stamp.

const callCache = new Map<string, { raw: string; parsed: ParsedCall[] }>();

export function parseToolCalls(msg: MessageRow): ParsedCall[] {

if (!msg.tool_calls) return [];

const hit = callCache.get(msg.id);

if (hit && hit.raw === msg.tool_calls) return hit.parsed;

let parsed: ParsedCall[] = [];

try {

parsed = JSON.parse(msg.tool_calls) as ParsedCall[];

} catch {}

callCache.set(msg.id, { raw: msg.tool_calls, parsed });

return parsed;

}

Reduce reported: 40,000 + 16,000 = 56,000 > 55,705. reported 38,000: 54,000 < 55,705 ✓ and > 0.6×65,536 = 39,322 ✓. So fillSession(60, 1000, 38000) works for that test.

export function modelBudget(model: string): ModelInfo {

return lookupModel(model);

+/**

+ * Current context size as measured + estimated (the opencode model):

+ * measured is the provider's report at the last call (lastPromptTokens,

+ * which already folds cache reads into the prompt); estimated is a chars/4

+ * tally of every visible node appended after that call, which the report does

+ * not cover. The report alone lags the live window by everything added since

+ * it, and the estimate alone misses system-prompt/tool-schema overhead the

+ * report captures — summed they track the window far better than either.

+ */

+export function sessionContextTokens(sessionId: string): number {

+ const measured = lastPromptTokens(sessionId);

+ const vis = visibleNodes(projectView(sessionId));

+ // newest-first scan; the tail since the last measured call is at most the

+ // last few turns, so this stops almost immediately in practice

+ let estimated = 0;

+ for (let i = vis.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {

+ const n = vis[i];

+ if (n.msg.role === "assistant" && n.msg.tool_calls) {

+ const p = n.msg.parent_id;

+ if (p && vis.some((m) => m.msg.id === p && m.msg.role === "user")) continue;

+ }

+ estimated += nodeTokenEstimate(n);

+ if (estimated >= measured) break;

+ }

+ return measured + estimated;

+}

+/** Estimated tokens a single node costs to send: content, its [N] marker,

+ * per-message framing, attachments, and any tool-call arguments. */

+export function nodeTokenEstimate(n: ViewNode): number {

+ let total = estimateTokens(n.content) + estimateTokens(marker(n.msg.seq)) + 4;

+ // flat per-attachment estimate, matching what turn.ts bills at append time

+ if (n.msg.media) total += 1500;

+ if (n.msg.role === "assistant" && n.msg.tool_calls) {

+ for (const c of parseToolCalls(n.msg)) total += estimateTokens(c.arguments);

}

return total;

}

Status

 

The bug we chased: your kimi-code-plan-cn provider under-reports the prompt size, so fox-agent never compacted — the stuck session mv0ucgs0cd9d3caa grew to ~2.1M tokens until the provider rejected it at its 1M limit.

 

Probes established the endpoint's real behavior:

- Small fully-cached prompt (88 tok): prompt_tokens: 88, cached_tokens: 88 → looked like "uncached-only."

- Large unique prompt, 20000 words (~29227 by chars/4): prompt_tokens: 20092 — so it's a ~1-token/word count, ~25% under chars/4.

- Same payload again (cache hit): prompt_tokens: 20092, cached_tokens: 20092 → prompt_tokens is the TOTAL; cached_tokens is a subset flag, not an additive bucket.

 

So summing prompt + cached (my first attempt) would double-count. I reverted lastPromptTokens to read prompt_tokens only.

 

What's actually implemented now (working tree, uncommitted — you rebuilt on top of it):

- src/context/render.ts — extracted nodeTokenEstimate(n) (content + marker + framing + media + tool args).

- src/context/budget.ts — new sessionContextTokens(sessionId) = last report + chars/4 estimate of visible nodes appended since (measured + estimated, opencode-style). checkBudget now uses it.

- src/context/compact.ts — compactIfNeeded trigger now uses it (fires on combined, not raw report).

- src/tui/app.ts — status bar ctx % uses it (dropped the now-unused storedPromptTokens alias).

- test/compact.test.ts — added "cache reads count toward measured" (now stale — see below) and "context size adds a chars/4 estimate of text since last report" (valid). Updated the threshold test.

 

Where I stopped: the threshold test a lower compactAt threshold triggers on a smaller view was failing because my comment said "raw report under 0.6" but the combined ~63k is actually over 0.85·65536=55705. I read the current file (lines 136-146) but have not yet applied the fix to that test — and the "cache reads count toward measured" test asserts the now-reverted 500+9500=10000 behavior and must be updated (with lastPromptTokens reading only prompt_tokens, a cache-hit report should read 500, not 10000).

 

Verification so far: bun run typecheck passed (before the db.ts revert). Full bun test not yet run after the revert.

 

I also notice your metadata now reads 125461/1048576 (12%) — materially higher than the ~83k "8%" readings earlier, so the rebuilt binary is indeed producing a larger (more honest) figure. That matches the delta-estimate kicking in.

 

Next: update those two stale tests to match the verified provider behavior, then run bun test test/compact.test.ts + full typecheck. Want me to proceed?

Typecheck: clean. Full test suite: 802 pass, 0 fail across 58 files. The 11 compaction tests all pass.

 

The metadata reading (11% provider-reported) is still the live bug — this endpoint tokenizes at ~1 token/word, so the real context is materially larger than 110500. The fix corrects exactly that.

 

What the fix does

 

sessionContextTokens(sessionId) (new, in src/context/budget.ts) now returns max(provider report, chars/4 estimate of the whole visible history), instead of trusting the provider's report alone. That single function feeds all three places that used to read the raw report:

 

• Compaction trigger (compactIfNeeded) — fires on the combined figure, so a loosely-tokenizing endpoint can no longer keep the count artificially low forever.

• checkBudget — the agent's "context nearly full" nudge uses the same honest number.

• TUI status bar (ctx %) — shows max(report, estimate) instead of the under-counted report.

 

Key design points, all validated by probing your provider:

- prompt_tokens is the total, not the uncached subset. A fully cache-hit call repeats the full size in cached_tokens (a subset flag), so summing the two would double-count. lastPromptTokens reads prompt_tokens only.

- max, not report + estimate, because both the report and the estimate are totals of the same visible history — adding them double-counts. The earlier measured + delta-since-anchor version under-counted precisely in the under-reporting case.

- The estimate reuses the exact per-node cost (nodeTokenEstimate) the renderer already bills: content + [N] marker + framing + attachments + tool-call args, so the figure matches what actually goes on the wire.

 

Files touched

• src/context/budget.ts — sessionContextTokens + checkBudget uses it

• src/context/compact.ts — trigger uses it

• src/context/render.ts — extracted nodeTokenEstimate

• src/tui/app.ts — status bar uses it; dropped unused storedPromptTokens alias

• test/compact.test.ts — updated the stale threshold test; added coverage that cache-hit reports don't double-count and that the estimate reflects text beyond the report

 

The working tree is uncommitted. Want me to commit and push this?

import { lookupModel } from "../providers/models.ts";

import type { ToolDef } from "../providers/types.ts";

import { renderTodos, getTodos } from "../tools/todo.ts";

import { VERSION } from "../core/version.ts";

import { shellPath } from "../core/shell.ts";

import os from "node:os";

 

export { VERSION };

 

/**

* Names of the tools that are actually callable this step.

*

* Every section below is gated on this rather than written as prose, because a

* prompt that describes a tool the registry doesn't have is worse than saying

* nothing: a subagent used to be handed the whole "context window management"

* doctrine while ctx was excluded from its registry, so its only possible

* move was to call a tool that did not exist.

*/

function toolNames(tools: ToolDef[]): Set<string> {

return new Set(tools.map((t) => t.name));

}

 

/** Provider-reported context size, see checkBudget. */

export interface RuntimeBudget {

reported: number;

limit: number;

ratio: number;

over: boolean;

}

 

/**

* The cache prefix: identity, project instructions, tool roster, doctrine,

* style — and nothing else.

*

* A provider's automatic prefix cache (and our Anthropic cache_control

* breakpoints) match from byte 0 forward, so a single changed byte in this

* string re-bills the system block AND every message behind it. That makes

* step-stability a correctness requirement, not an optimization: the only

* things allowed in here are those that change when the toolset or the project

* instructions change. The clock, the todo list, cwd, the model name and the

* live budget figure used to live here — the last one moves on every step —

* which is why a 1.6k system prompt cost a fresh 1.6k re-read 5,157 times in a

* row. Those all travel in buildRuntimeHeader() at the message tail instead.

*/

import { agentDocsDir, ensureAgentDocs } from "../core/selfdocs.ts";

 

export function buildSystemPrompt(

opts: {

tools: ToolDef[];

projectInstructions?: string;

},

): string {

const have = toolNames(opts.tools);

const sections: string[] = [];

 

sections.push(You are fox-agent, a light coding harness with full machine control — no permission prompts. Work directly and verify your changes.);

 

if (opts.projectInstructions) sections.push(## Project instructions\n${opts.projectInstructions});

 

// Names only. The provider already sends every tool's full description and

// JSON schema in the API tool block, so restating them here bought nothing —

// and the old formatter cut each one at its first ". ", which silently dropped

// load-bearing clauses (exec's "working directory never carries over" among

// them) and truncated glob mid-abbreviation at "(e.g". What is left is the

// roster plus the two contracts no JSON schema can express.

const roster = [## Tools, Full descriptions and JSON schemas arrive with the API tool definitions — read them there.];

roster.push(Available now: ${opts.tools.map((t) => t.name).join(", ")});

if (have.has("exec")) roster.push(- exec never drifts: every call starts in the session directory, and \workdir\ is per-call, never sticky.);

if (have.has("pty")) roster.push(- pty is one persistent shell that KEEPS its working directory, environment and processes between calls.);

if (have.has("repl")) roster.push(- repl is an in-process JS scratchpad with persistent vars; reach tools from code as tools.call(name, args) — direct calls bypass beforeTool/afterTool hooks.);

sections.push(roster.join("\n"));

 

if (have.has("ctx")) {

sections.push(

[

## Context window management (your core ability)\n +

Every message in your view carries a stable marker [N]. Large old tool outputs are dead weight — query, don't re-read:\n +

- find nodes first: {"op":"search","pattern":"error"} shows snippets, never bodies\n +

- after using a big result, hide it: {"op":"delete","ids":[3,5],"summary":"ran build; fixed 2 errors"}\n +

/**

* session, and os.cpus() walks the machine's CPU list (sysctl on macOS,

* /proc/cpuinfo on Linux), which is not worth four syscalls on every step.

*/

let machine: { host: string; os: string; runtime: string } | undefined;

function machineFacts(): { host: string; os: string; runtime: string } {

if (machine) return machine;

const versions = process.versions as Record<string, string | undefined>;

machine = {

host: os.hostname(),

// one line rather than four keys: platform/kernel/arch, parallelism (so

// the agent can decide how much to fan out) and the shell that exec and

// pty actually run in — all of "what box am I on" in a dozen tokens

os: ${process.platform} ${os.release()} ${os.arch()} · ${os.cpus().length} cpu · shell=${shellPath()},

runtime: versions.bun ? bun ${versions.bun} : node ${process.version},

};

return machine;

}

 

/**

* Local wall clock, minute granularity. The tail is rebuilt every step anyway

* so the ticking costs nothing extra, and an agent that cannot answer the

* question "what time is it" burns an exec date finding out.

*

* The offset uses UTC+8 / UTC-5:30 notation rather than a raw +08:00 — it reads

* as a zone, not as a timestamp, and it cannot be mistaken for part of the date.

*/

function localClock(): { date: string; tz: string } {

const now = new Date();

const p2 = (n: number) => String(n).padStart(2, "0");

const mins = -now.getTimezoneOffset();

const abs = Math.abs(mins);

const offset =

mins === 0 ? "UTC" : UTC${mins < 0 ? "-" : "+"}${Math.floor(abs / 60)}${abs % 60 ? :${p2(abs % 60)} : ""};

const zone = Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone || offset;

return {

date: ${now.getFullYear()}-${p2(now.getMonth() + 1)}-${p2(now.getDate())},

tz: zone === offset ? offset : ${zone} ${offset},

};

}

* catalog preset id; format is the wire API. Both go to the model: the first

* says which quota pool and vendor quirks apply, the second says what protocol

* it is actually speaking (which is what decides caching and tool behaviour).

*/

function providerLine(p?: { name?: string; format?: string }): string {

const name = p?.name;

const format = p?.format;

if (name && format && name !== format) return ${name} (${format});

return name ?? format ?? "unknown";

}

// MCP client bridge: connects configured stdio servers, merges their tools

// into the registry under mcp<server><tool>. The SDK is a dynamic import

// so fox-agent still runs (without MCP) if it isn't installed.

import type { McpServerConfig } from "../core/config.ts";

import type { MediaPart, ToolDef } from "../providers/types.ts";

import type { Tool, ToolResult } from "./types.ts";

import { fail, ok } from "./types.ts";

import { childEnv } from "../core/childenv.ts";

import { VERSION } from "../core/version.ts";

 

const OUTCAPMCP = 30_000;

 

/** Live clients, so shutdownTools() can reap the stdio children. */

interface LiveClient {

close: () => Promise<void>;

/** the stdio child's pid — closeMcp SIGKILLs it when a polite close hangs */

pid?: number;

}

let cache: { key: string; tools: Map<string, Tool>; warnings: string[]; clients: LiveClient[] } | null = null;

 

/**

* MCP content parts -> ToolResult. Text joins as output; image parts become

* real MediaParts so a vision-capable model sees the picture instead of a

* JSON-stringified base64 blob (which is how chrome-devtools screenshots

* used to arrive — megabytes of base64 as plain text).

*/

function toResult(content: unknown, isError: boolean): ToolResult {

const parts = content as { type?: string; text?: string; data?: string; mimeType?: string }[] | null;

if (!Array.isArray(parts)) {

const s = JSON.stringify(content ?? {});

return isError ? fail(s) : ok(s);

}

const text: string[] = [];

const media: MediaPart[] = [];

for (const p of parts) {

if (p?.type === "image" && typeof p.data === "string") {

media.push({ mimeType: p.mimeType ?? "image/png", data: p.data });

} else if (typeof p?.text === "string") {

text.push(p.text);

} else {

text.push(JSON.stringify(p));

}

}

const base = isError ? fail(text.join("\n").slice(0, OUTCAPMCP)) : ok(text.join("\n").slice(0, OUTCAPMCP));

return media.length ? { ...base, media } : base;

}

Why capitalized words highlight, and how a real lib helps

 

The bug is in src/tui/highlight.ts. It uses this token regex:

 

│ const TOKEN = /(\/\/.*$|#.*$|--.*$)|("...string...")|(\b\d...\b)|(\b[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\b)/g;

│ // group 4 ──────────────── every identifier

 

Every identifier hits group 4. Then the tail of the matcher (around line 70+) does roughly: if it's in the KEYWORDS set → tint it the keyword color; else if it starts with a capital → tint it as a "type/class". That catch-all is the problem — it's meant for Foo, Bar in code, but it fires on any** capitalized word, including sentence-start words in prose.

 

And In, Self, This, By are in the KEYWORDS set because that set is a union of ~8 languages' keywords (JS in/this, Rust Self, Python this-by-convention…). So plain prose gets tinted as if it were code.

 

A real highlighting lib fixes this properly because it doesn't guess — it parses. Libraries like Shiki, highlight.js, or syntect (the Rust engine, via a WASM/Node binding):

- Build an actual syntax tree, so they know In at the start of an English sentence is not the JS in operator.

- Use real TextMate/Tree-sitter grammars — context-sensitive, not a flat regex + capital-letter heuristic.

- Already handle the "is this a keyword here?" question correctly per-language.

 

The tradeoff: fox-agent's current highlighter is dependency-free and line-local (re-runs per frame, cheap). A real lib is heavier (WASM grammars, more CPU per frame) — you'd typically pre-tokenize once per fence block, not per frame, to keep it fast.

 

But the cheapest correct fix is a small patch to the existing matcher: only apply the "capitalized → type" tint when the fence language is actually a code language (not text/prose), and drop the cross-language KEYWORDS union for ambiguous words. That kills the prose highlighting without adding a dependency.

 

Which do you want: (a) the minimal patch to the current regex highlighter, or (b) integrate a real grammar-based lib (Shiki/highlight.js)?

fox-agent — roadmap & decisions

 

fox-agent (fox) — light coding harness with agent-controlled context. Built to be used for building itself (dogfooding).

Repo: github.com/QQSHI13/fox-agent · local ~/.openclaw/workspace/projects/fox-agent · binary bin/fox (+ sidecar libopentui.so) · npm fox-agent

 

Identity

• Name: foxc → renamed fox-agent (npm blocked "foxc" as too similar to solc; CLI is fox) (npm/PyPI/brew free at planning time; GitHub user taken = irrelevant)

• Avoided trademark traps: qodex (~Codex), foxcode/openfox (taken), clawd-style near-misses

 

Locked design decisions

│ Area │ Decision │

├────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

│ Language │ TypeScript on Bun (one language core→TUI→plugins→future web) │

│ Core │ ~80-line agent loop; everything else = tools/hooks │

│ Tools v1 │ read, write, edit, glob, grep, exec (one-shot + persistent pty via tmux), │

│ │ ctx_edit │

│ Context │ inline [mN] markers on every message; NO history_list tool — LLM sees IDs │

│ │ natively │

│ ctx_edit │ batched delete(+summary placeholder)/replace ops; view-only, storage │

│ │ immutable │

│ Sessions │ SQLite WAL, INSERT-only message DAG (parent_id), refs table │

│ │ (branches/reverts), ops table (view surgery events), failures logged as │

│ │ rows │

│ Permissions │ NONE — pi-style full control; env passthrough │

│ Providers │ tokenguard gateway first (one URL+key, OpenAI-compatible); thin Provider │

│ │ port for direct mode │

│ Runtime header │ cwd/git/os/date/model/version injected per prompt build, moved to BOTTOM │

│ │ of system prompt │

│ UI │ wrapper-first TUI on @opentui/solid (user rejected linear-stream: needs │

│ │ owned viewport for history rewrite + tty-without-scrollback) │

 

Roadmap

• v1 — DONE: agent loop · tools (read/write/edit/glob/grep/exec/pty/ctx_edit/todowrite/task/fetch) · SQLite sessions+refs+ops · runtime header · streaming OpenAI-compatible provider · TUI · slash commands · ! shell mode · \ escape syntax · MCP client (live-tested 2026-08 against a real stdio server, test/mcp.test.ts)

• v1.5 — DONE: Plugin API — src/plugins/, one module registers tools + lifecycle hooks (onSessionStart/beforeLLMCall/afterTool) + custom providers

• v2 — DONE: ACP server (fox --acp) · ACP client (what task is built on) · LSP integration (diagnostics, TS/Python/Rust built in). Closed 2026-08 by scripts/acp-accept.ts, an acceptance check driving the compiled binary with the real external acpx client.

• v3 (next, deferred): A2A delegation · OpenAI-compatible endpoint (serve fox-agent as a model) · web UI

 

Roadmap history: originally ACP-first; reordered wrapper-first because history rewrite is the core feature and terminals have scroll limits. v1.5 was skipped past at the time and picked back up after v2 closed.

 

Plugin trust decision (do not reopen)

Plugins load from ~/.config/fox/config.toml only. A plugins key in a project fox.toml is ignored with

a warning naming both files. Reason: every other extension point ([mcpServers.*], [agents.*], [lsp.*])

spawns a child through childEnv(), which strips *_API_KEY/FOX_AUTH*. A plugin cannot be sandboxed that

way — it is imported into fox's own process and inherits the whole environment, API key included. So

"clone a repo, cd in, run fox" must not execute that repo's code. This is why applyTable takes a

scope: "global" | "project" parameter, which it needs for exactly this one key, and why Config grew a

warnings: string[] (there had to be somewhere to put the message — silence is the one outcome you cannot

debug). Verified against the compiled binary, not just a unit test.

 

Hooks are patch-based and additive. beforeLLMCall returns {appendSystem?}, afterTool returns

{output?}. Neither can reorder or drop messages, so renderContext's invariant (every assistant

tool_call followed by its tool_result) holds by construction — a hook returning a message array would

hand that invariant to plugin authors, and breaking it surfaces as a provider 400 that names nothing.

afterTool runs between execToolCall and appendMessage, so the patched text is the only version stored,

shown to the model, and reported via tool_end.

 

Hard-won technical facts (do not relearn these)

• Bun's JSX transform is react-style → must build with @opentui/solid/bun-plugin (babel-preset-solid) or nothing reactive works; opencode uses vite for the same reason

• Compiled binary + FFI: ship libopentui.so beside binary and call setRenderLibPath() before renderer creation (two-step build: bundle w/ plugin → bun build --compile dist/cli.js)

• Mark other-platform @opentui/core-* natives as external in Bun.build

• OpenAI wire format: toolcalls must nest {id,type:"function",function:{name,arguments}}; every toolcall needs a following tool msg (pairing repair needed after surgery)

• Deleting tool results requires hiding parent assistant's tool_call too (orphan repair in context renderer)

• clipboardy/execa crashes bun-compiled binaries → OSC52 + powershell/wl-copy/xclip spawners instead

• opentui textarea won't take focus reliably → custom input on global useKeyboard; exitOnCtrlC must be disabled for smart ctrl+c

• zen gateway streams reasoning_content deltas (thinking)

• acpx --json-strict does not police the agent. It suppresses acpx's own non-JSON stderr. acpx's stdout under --format json is acpx's reconstruction of the conversation, and its ndjson reader silently skips an agent line it cannot parse — so a stray console.log in fox's ACP server is invisible from acpx's output. Stdout purity can only be proved by a direct spawn-and-read of fox's own stdout. Found by sabotage: a console.log in runAcpServer left all checks green.

• acpx needs the exec subcommand; a bare prompt exits 4 NO_SESSION because it wants a pre-existing acpx-managed session record.

• In-process protocol tests share assumptions. All 31 ACP tests use client().connectWith(buildAgent(...)) — same SDK objects on both ends, so a wrong field name or a mishandled advertised capability passes every one. Only a foreign client proves the wire format.

• Bun's module registry caches a dynamically imported plugin and resetPlugins() cannot clear it. Anything a plugin reads from process.env at module scope freezes to the first caller's value — read it per call.

• A compiled binary cannot load a plugin that imports from src/. A plugin fixture used with bin/fox must depend only on node builtins (or the published package), which is also the position a real user's plugin is in.

Deferred: Anthropic cache TTL — decided 2026-10-04, deliberately NOT in this round

 

Skip ttl: "1h" for now and measure first: the cached_tokens plumbing (hit rate in /usage and in

the status bar) lands in this round, and the TTL call gets made against a real hit rate rather than

against arithmetic alone. Do not quietly fold the TTL change into that commit.

 

What was established — don't re-derive it:

 

• Mixed TTLs are legal, but ordered: a longer-TTL breakpoint must come BEFORE a shorter one. Two

independent sources agree — an API FAQ ("Yes, but with constraints. Longer TTL breakpoints must come

before shorter ones.") and agno's docs, which call a 5m block preceding a 1h block a violation of

"Anthropic's mixed-TTL ordering rule". src/providers/anthropic.ts marks rest[len-2] (stable) and

rest[len-1] (runtime tail), i.e. the earlier index first, so 1h → 5m is the legal order and every

candidate shape below is valid.

- Pricing: 5m write 1.25x, 1h write 2x, read 0.1x either way. The TTL refreshes free on every hit, so

an active turn never expires it — only an idle gap does, and those live at turn boundaries (a human

reading a diff for six minutes). Break-even: one avoided re-write per hour covers the 2x premium

(0.75P paid once, ~0.9P saved per avoided re-write at prompt size P).

- Today's two breakpoints are not equivalent. rest[len-1] is the ephemeral runtime tail, rewritten

every step, so that entry is never read — it is a pure 1.25x write. rest[len-2] is the last stable

history message, the one every subsequent step actually reads. Candidate shapes, cheapest first:

stable 1h + tail left at 5m (legal, minimal) / both 1h (no mixing, tail write goes to 2x) / drop the

tail breakpoint entirely and put 1h on the stable one alone (optimal; needs a length guard, and no

production caller lacks a tail).

- OpenCode (~/opencode-v2) ships none of it: packages/ai/src/cache-policy.ts, default policy

"auto" = last tool + first and last system parts + conversation tail, capped at 4 breakpoints (the

Anthropic API 400s past that). No ttl on the wire by default — ttlBucket() only emits "1h" when

ttlSeconds >= 3600 — and there is no user config surface for the knob. It does capture

cacheReadInputTokens/cacheWriteInputTokens into tokens.cache.{read,write}, aggregates and costs

them, but shows no hit rate anywhere in its UI.

1. Quota / usage display

• No documented /usage command in v2 TUI (command list: connect, compact, details, editor, export,

init, models, new, redo, sessions, share, themes, thinking, undo, unshare). Usage surfaces live in

the status/context area + provider dashboards; docs are thin here.

- OpenCode Zen: pay-per-request credits, auto-reload when balance drops below $5, and workspace-level

AND per-member monthly usage limits ("set a monthly usage limit to $20, Zen will not use more than

$20 in a month"). OpenCode Go = low-cost subscription plan. Deprecated-models table per provider.

- Context management is a hidden compaction agent (primary mode, not selectable) that auto-compacts

long context; users can also /compact (alias /summarize).

- fox-agent shows ctx N% (xk/yk) · cache N% but has no per-message/session cost estimate, no provider

plan-limit/quota display, and no remaining-until-compact indicator.

→ fox-agent: add a cost-per-session estimate + provider quota line to the status bar; auto-compact threshold is the more valuable steal.

 

2. ChatGPT subscription without an API key (Codex)

From codex.ts — it's OAuth 2.0 + PKCE against OpenAI's auth issuer, NOT an API key:

- issuer https://auth.openai.com, clientid `appEMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann` (Codex CLI's client id)

- authorize URL params: response_type=code, scope="openid profile email offline_access",

code_challenge_method=S256, codex_cli_simplified_flow=true, originator=opencode

- redirect: opencode spins a local HTTP server on port 1455 and serves an OAuth callback page

- token exchange + refresh: POST {issuer}/oauth/token with PKCE verifier / refresh_token grant

- inference goes to https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses (Responses API), chatgptaccountid

extracted from id_token JWT claims (chatgpt_account_id or https://api.openai.com/auth)

- stored in ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json (chmod 0600) as `{type:"oauth", refresh, access,

expires, accountId}; auth store also supports {type:"api", key} and {type:"wellknown"}`;

OPENCODE_AUTH_CONTENT env can inject the whole auth JSON

- client-side model allowlist (gpt-5.x set) with gpt-5.5-pro explicitly disallowed

→ fox-agent: replicable in ~100 lines — loopback listener + PKCE S256 + refresh persisted 0600; same pattern works for any OAuth-native subscription backend.

• /connect → "GitHub Copilot" → standard GitHub OAuth device flow: opens

github.com/login/device, user enters code like 8F43-6FCF, TUI polls until authorized.

- Stored as the oauth auth record (supports enterpriseUrl for GHES). Models are then picked via

/models; some need a Copilot Pro+ plan.

- Transport: a vendored in-repo openai-compatible AI SDK provider

(packages/core/src/github-copilot/ with chat + responses paths) pointing at Copilot's endpoints.

→ fox-agent: GitHub device flow + a thin openai-compatible provider shim = Copilot support; reuse for GHES.

• webfetch: built-in, permission-gated ("fetch and read web pages").

OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA=1 / OPENCODE_ENABLE_PARALLEL=1. Backend is Exa or Parallel's hosted MCP

5. LSP integration

• Off by default. lsp: true enables all built-ins, lsp: {} keeps built-ins + add overrides.

• ~35 built-in servers keyed by file extension (typescript, pyright, rust-analyzer, gopls, eslint,

vue, svelte, yaml...); some auto-install (astro, terraform, yaml, kotlin, lua, php); others need the

toolchain on PATH. OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD=true blocks auto-download.

- On file open: match extension → start server if not running. **Diagnostics are fed back to the

agent as feedback.**

- Config shape: `lsp: { "<name>": { disabled?, command: string[], extensions: string[], env?,

initialization? } }` (initialization = server-specific init options, e.g. intelephense prefs).

- Experimental lsp tool (OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_LSP_TOOL=true) exposes goToDefinition,

findReferences, hover, documentSymbol, workspaceSymbol, goToImplementation, call hierarchy.

- Honest best-practices note in docs: LSP often isn't a net positive (drift, memory, version skew);

letting the agent run lint/typecheck CLIs is frequently better — enable only when it helps.

→ fox-agent: we already feed diagnostics (v2, TS/Python/Rust); steal the on-demand lsp navigation tool behind an env flag + the opt-in default-off stance.

 

6. Share / link feature

• /share creates opncd.ai/s/<share-id>: unique public URL, conversation history + metadata synced

to their servers, link copied to clipboard. /unshare deletes it.

• Config share: "manual" (default) | "auto" (every new session shared) | "disabled"

(project-checked-in opencode.json enforces it for a team).

- Enterprise: disable entirely, restrict to SSO users, or self-host.

- Data retention: stays public until explicitly unshared.

→ fox-agent: nice-to-have only; if built, manual-by-default + disabled mode + export-to-markdown (they also have /export) covers most of the value.

Self-documentation research (2026-10-07) — pi + opencode-v2

 

pi (github.com/earendil-works/pi, packages/coding-agent)

• Docs ship INSIDE the package: getPackageDir()/docs/*.md (~25 files: extensions, themes, keybindings, skills, sdk, tui, models, mcp, custom-provider...) + README + examples/. getPackageDir() = env PI_PACKAGE_DIR override, else resolved from the compiled binary path.

• The ONLY mechanism is a system-prompt routing section (system-prompt.ts ~162): "Pi documentation (read only when the user asks about pi itself...)" with a topic→file map (extensions → docs/extensions.md, themes → docs/themes.md, ...), plus rules: read docs completely, follow .md cross-references, resolve docs/... under the docs path not cwd.

• No special tool. The agent uses its ordinary read tool on real files. Skills do progressive disclosure the same way: name+description in prompt, SKILL.md read on demand.

 

opencode-v2 (~/opencode-v2)

• /init = a PROMPT TEMPLATE, not a tool: packages/core/src/plugin/command/initialize.txt (65 lines) injected as a user turn via the command plugin. Content: "Create or update AGENTS.md... every line should answer 'would an agent miss this without help?'... read highest-value sources first (README, manifests, build config, CI, existing instruction files)... prefer executable sources of truth over prose... only ask the user what the repo cannot answer... if AGENTS.md exists, improve in place — preserve verified guidance, delete fluff."

• Config self-edit: NO dedicated tool, NO system-prompt mention. The agent edits opencode.json with ordinary file tools; config discovery/validation picks it up. (pi same: config via docs + ordinary tools.)

 

→ fox-agent design (decided)

• fox compiles to ONE binary — no package dir to read docs from. So: author docs as .md files under docs/agent/ in the repo, EMBED them at build time (bun text imports), MATERIALIZE to agentHome()/docs/ at startup (version-stamped dir, rewrite when version changes) so the agent's read tool sees real paths.

• buildSystemPrompt gains a "Self documentation" section (pi-style routing): "read only when the user asks about fox-agent itself" + topic→file map (config, plugins, tools, acp, themes, keybindings/TUI, sessions).

• /init slash command = opencode-style template (adapted: fox-agent.toml + AGENTS.md, mentions validate callbacks throw, global-only plugins) injected as a user turn via runAgent.

• Config self-edit needs nothing special — the agent already has write/edit + /reload exists. The docs routing section is what makes the agent KNOW it can.

 

Domain + plugin market + session export/share (2026-10-08)

 

Domain for a future plugin/extension market

• Recommendation: foxagent.dev (short, clean; .dev enforces HTTPS — good for a registry that

serves install manifests). Register also fox-agent.dev (people will type the dash; 301 it).

- Fallbacks in order: foxagent.sh (CLI-flavored), getfox.dev (the "get<pattern>"), foxagent.io if

.dev taken. Avoid .ai (expensive renewal, screams "wrapper").

- Architecture note: the market does NOT need the domain to be a hosted service on day one.

Phase 1: an awesome-fox-agent GitHub repo — curated TOML/JS plugin list with one-line

descriptions, categories, install = paste a path/URL into global config plugins.entries.

Zero infrastructure, review via PRs, the same way awesome-* lists and clawhub's early days work.

Phase 2: when volume justifies it, registry service on the domain (manifests + tarballs +

fox install <name>), and the awesome repo becomes the curated front page pointing at it.

- ClawHub precedent worth copying: slug-based install (clawhub install <slug>), but keep

fox-agent's rule that plugins load from GLOBAL config only (security boundary — the market

must never make project-local plugin loading look sanctioned).

 

Session export/share design (how opencode/pi do it, and the fox shape)

• opencode: server-side share — opencode share uploads the session to their cloud, returns

a URL; sync data model with an explicit share object; /unshare revokes. Requires a server.

- pi: export-html package — LOCAL static HTML render of the session (template.html/css/js

in core/export-html, tool renderer hooks so plugins can render their own tool calls). No

server, no account; the file is yours to host anywhere. SessionManager entries → HTML.

- → fox-agent (decided shape): pi-style local export first, no service.

1. /export exists already (markdown). Add /share = self-contained HTML file written to

cwd (or --out): session rendered with the TUI's own theme colors (getResolvedThemeColors

pattern), syntax-highlighted code blocks, tool calls collapsed/expandable (details/summary),

images inlined as data URIs. Static single file, no JS dependencies, works offline.

2. Optional public path = user hosts the file themselves ( gist, S3, their site). No fox server,

no phone-home, nothing to trust. If a hosted share is ever wanted, it's a THIRD-PARTY plugin

(share-to-<service>) — the core never uploads transcripts anywhere (privacy rule).

3. Implementation seam: the session store already has allMessagesLite(); an exporter walks

items → HTML via a small renderer; reuse the markdown/highlight code from the TUI row

renderer where possible; a plugin-style renderer hook so bundled tool plugins can render

their calls/results (pi's ToolHtmlRenderer pattern).

Summing `prompt + cached` double-counts every cache hit.\n- Small fully-cached prompt (88 tok) → `prompt_tokens: 88, cached_tokens: 88` (looked like \"uncached-only\" but the large-prompt probe disproves that).\n\nFix (`84f34e1`, rebased to `f510d26`): new `sessionContextTokens(sessionId)` in `src/context/budget.ts` returns `max(lastPromptTokens, chars/4 estimate of the whole visible history)`. `max`, not `report + delta`, because both are totals of the same history. Notes updated. Now the three answers.

 

Shorter domain suggestions

 

Current pick is foxagent.dev. Shorter options, best first:

 

│ domain │ len │ note │

├───────────────────┼─────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

│ fox.sh │ 6 │ shortest clean one; .sh signals CLI/shell, devs trust it │

│ fox.dev │ 7 │ taken-risk (single common word), but ideal if free │

│ fxa.dev │ 7 │ initials, very short, almost certainly free │

│ foxa.dev │ 8 │ near-match of the name, likely free │

│ foxagent.io │ 11 │ your fallback, drop .dev for .io (same length as foxagent.dev) │

 

My recommendation: fox.sh if you want maximal brevity and the CLI identity; fxa.dev if you want short + the enforce-HTTPS .dev registry benefit. Grab whichever is free.

 

opencode-study takeaways (the actionable ones)

 

From the 2026-10-07 study of opencode-v2 + pi, ranked by "cheap to steal, high value":

 

1. Git-backed /undo + /redo — restores conversation and file changes via git snapshotting (needs a git repo).

2. Hidden system agents — a title and summary agent (mode primary, hidden: true) auto-generates session titles/summaries; also a hidden compaction agent. fox-agent's auto-compaction is host-driven, but title/summary is an easy steal.

3. On-demand lsp nav tool behind an env flag — goToDefinition/findReferences/hover/etc. (opencode's is experimental + default-off; their docs even admit LSP often isn't a net win vs letting the agent run lint/typecheck CLIs).

4. question tool — model asks the user structured questions mid-run (fox-agent already has question).

5. Cost-per-session + provider-quota line in the status bar — opencode shows no hit rate in its UI; this is a place to beat them.

6. Markdown-defined project agents — agents/<name>.md with frontmatter (description/mode/model/permission), plus the multi-agent split (Build/Plan primaries, Explore/Scout subagents).

7. apply_patch tool — multi-file patch text (Add/Update/Move/Delete), codex-style.

8. ChatGPT-subscription / Copilot auth — both are just OAuth (PKCE / device flow) + a thin openai-compatible shim; replicable in ~100 lines each.

9. /init as a prompt template (not a tool) for writing AGENTS.md — fox-agent already decided this shape.

10. Local-first share/export — pi-style self-contained HTML, no server; a hosted share would only ever be a third-party plugin.

 

Also worth noting: opencode deliberately has no permissions by default (Plan agent is just permission config), same philosophy as fox-agent.

/**

* The built-in tools that ship AS plugins. Same FoxPlugin shape a third-party

* module exports, loaded through the same merge path in buildRegistry, so:

*

* - a user plugin can shadow one of these by name (later registration wins,

* with a warning) exactly the way it shadows any other tool;

* - disabledPlugins = ["pty"] turns one off without touching code;

* - the pty plugin demonstrates the lifecycle seam: its tmux session is

* released from onSessionEnd, not from a special case in the harness.

* - the repl plugin demonstrates the same seam for lighter state: its

* per-session scratchpad is dropped from onSessionEnd.

*/

import type { FoxPlugin } from "./types.ts";

import { ptyDef, drivePty, cleanupPty, ptySessionName } from "../tools/pty.ts";

import { todoDef, todoRun } from "../tools/todo.ts";

import { fetchDef, fetchRun } from "../tools/fetch.ts";

import { replDef, replRun, cleanupRepl } from "../tools/repl.ts";

import { questionPlugin } from "../tools/question.ts";

import { lspPlugin } from "../tools/lsp.ts";

import costPlugin, { costSegment } from "./cost.ts";

 

const ptyPlugin: FoxPlugin = {

name: "bundled:pty",

tools: [{ def: ptyDef, run: drivePty }],

hooks: {

// tmux sessions outlive the fox-agent turn that made them; the hook is what

// ties their lifetime to the session's, on exit AND on session switch

onSessionEnd: (c) => cleanupPty(ptySessionName(c.sessionId)),

},

};

 

const todoPlugin: FoxPlugin = { name: "bundled:todo", tools: [{ def: todoDef, run: todoRun }] };

const fetchPlugin: FoxPlugin = { name: "bundled:fetch", tools: [{ def: fetchDef, run: fetchRun }] };

 

const replPlugin: FoxPlugin = {

name: "bundled:repl",

tools: [{ def: replDef, run: replRun }],

hooks: {

// the scratchpad is per-session memory; drop it with the session

onSessionEnd: (c) => cleanupRepl(c.sessionId),

},

};

 

/** All bundled plugins. Order matters only for shadowing: user plugins load after. */

export function bundledPlugins(): FoxPlugin[] {

return [ptyPlugin, todoPlugin, fetchPlugin, replPlugin, questionPlugin, lspPlugin, costPlugin];

}

* The cost plugin's TUI segment. Lives beside the plugin (not inside it)

* because plugin statusSegments resolve without session context; the TUI

* calls this per frame with the active session. disabledPlugins keeps it

* consistent: disabling bundled:cost removes the tally everywhere.

*/

export { costSegment };

New format fully live, and the context fix is working (ctx: 99590 now reflects the estimate path, not just the raw report). Bun's native Bun.TOML.parse round-trips your config shape fine. Here are the three answers.

 

1. Bundled plugins vs. core

 

fox-agent splits its tools into hard-coded core and bundled plugins (same FoxPlugin shape a user module exports, loaded through the same merge path — so a user plugin can shadow them by name, and disabledPlugins = ["pty"] turns one off).

 

Bundled plugins (src/plugins/bundled.ts, each bundled:<name>):

│ plugin │ provides │ why it's a plugin (lifecycle seam) │

├────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤

│ pty │ pty tool │ tmux session released from onSessionEnd, │

│ │ │ not a harness special-case │

│ todo │ todo tool │ stateless │

│ fetch │ fetch tool │ stateless │

│ repl │ repl tool │ per-session scratchpad dropped from │

│ │ │ onSessionEnd │

│ question │ question tool │ structured mid-run questions │

│ lsp │ lsp tool │ LSP navigation/diagnostics │

│ cost │ cost tracking + TUI costSegment │ status-bar segment, disabled consistently │

│ │ │ with the plugin │

 

Core tools (src/tools/, hard-coded into the registry): read, write, edit (patch), glob, grep, exec, ctx (context surgery), task (subagent/ACP dispatch). Plus the MCP client bridge (src/tools/mcp.ts) which fans out into the mcp__<server>__<tool> tools.

 

The bundled ones are exactly the "cheap plugin" candidates you mentioned — they're already plugins, so shipping them as on-demand marketplace installs instead of bundled is mostly a packaging/default-enable decision, not new code.

 

2. What the ai dep does

 

ai (Vercel's AI SDK, v7) is the provider-agnostic orchestration layer. fox-agent's own provider files (src/providers/anthropic.ts, the openai-compatible one, etc.) build on it for: the unified LanguageModel request/response shape, streaming, tool-call parsing, and the provider-specific wire adapters via the @ai-sdk/* satellites (@ai-sdk/anthropic, @ai-sdk/openai, @ai-sdk/google, @ai-sdk/openai-compatible). Without it you'd hand-roll streaming + tool-call deltas + per-provider quirks. The MCP SDK (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk) is separate — that's the mcp bridge.

 

3. Bun 1.4.3 TOML vs smol-toml — yes, replace it

 

smol-toml is used in exactly one file, src/core/config.ts, in two places:

- parseTomlLib(text) at line 651 (read config)

- stringifyToml(doc) at line 645 (write config)

 

Bun 1.4.3 ships a native Bun.TOML module. I round-tripped your actual config shape through Bun.TOML.parse (top-level scalars + [providers.*] + [mcpServers.*] tables + inline env = {...}) and it parses correctly. Two caveats:

- Bun.TOML.parse exists; stringify is the gap. Bun's native TOML is parse-focused. For the write path (stringifyToml) you'd either keep smol-toml just for stringify, or write a small serializer (your config is a shallow, well-known shape — a ~15-line serializer covers it), or accept that fox-agent's own config writes become hand-formatted.

- Compiled-binary check: confirm Bun.TOML is exposed in the bun build --compile output (it should be, but verify against bin/fox, since some Bun.* internals are runtime-only).

 

Recommendation: drop smol-toml for Bun.TOML.parse, and either keep a tiny hand-rolled stringify or a minimal vendored serializer — net -1 dependency. Want me to do that swap, or leave it until you're trimming deps deliberately?

The new format is fully live and the context fix is working (ctx: 101151 — that's the estimate path, not the raw ~80k report). Here's the full Bun TOML audit.

 

Bun 1.4.3 TOML — full test results

 

Surface: Bun.TOML exposes both parse and stringify (you mentioned 1.4.1's stringify was broken — it's present in 1.4.3 and now works).

 

Parse — your real config shape: ✅

Top-level scalars (strings, bools, ints, floats), [providers.*], [mcpServers.*] with inline env = { K = "v", N = 8080 }, [agents.*] with disabledPlugins = [...] arrays — all parse to the correct JS types.

 

Parse — TOML spec edge cases: ✅

Multiline strings ("""), nested arrays ([[1,2],[3,4]]), mixed arrays, integers/floats. Datetimes parse to Temporal objects, not strings — 2026-10-12T10:00:00Z → Temporal.Instant, 2026-10-12 → Temporal.PlainDate, 10:00:00 → Temporal.PlainTime. That's spec-correct but a behavior difference from smol-toml (which gives plain strings). For fox-agent's config this doesn't matter — you don't use date keys — but it's the kind of thing that silently changes a value's type if you ever did.

 

Stringify — round-trip: ✅

Bun.TOML.stringify produced a 616-char string from the parsed config, and re-parsing it deep-equals the original. So parse → stringify → parse is stable.

 

Verdict: yes, replace smol-toml

 

Bun.TOML covers both call sites in src/core/config.ts (parseTomlLib at read, stringifyToml at write). The only behavioral note is the Temporal datetime objects, which fox-agent's config doesn't use. Net -1 dependency.

 

Two things to verify before committing to it in the compiled binary:

1. Bun.TOML must be exposed in the bun build --compile output — most Bun.* APIs are, but confirm against bin/fox.

2. Error messages on malformed TOML (fox-agent surfaces parse errors to the user on a bad config) — check Bun.TOML.parse's error shape is as actionable as smol-toml's line/col reporting.

│ 5-yr total │ ~$61 │ ~$65 │

│ HTTPS │ enforced (HSTS-preloaded) │ optional │

│ signal │ "developer tool" │ "consumer/mobile app" │

 

.dev wins on 5-year cost, enforced HTTPS (right for a registry serving install manifests), and it reads as a dev tool — which fox-agent is. .app only wins if you specifically want the mobile-app connotation, which you don't.

 

The catch with .dev

 

.dev is on the HSTS-preload list. That means any future non-HTTPS use of the domain is impossible — no plain-HTTP staging, no local dev server on it, every subdomain must have TLS from day one. For a package registry that's a feature, not a bug, but it's worth knowing before you commit.

 

What I'd actually do

 

Register fox-agent.dev now at Cloudflare, and grab foxagent.dev too if it's cheap (it's the no-dash typo and people will type it). Cloudflare renews at cost, so the $12.20 holds year over year. Skip the expensive fox.* — they're hundreds and mostly gone, and a two-word domain is honest about what the project is.

 

If you want insurance against the .dev HSTS lock-in ever mattering, register fox-agent.app as well — $8.20 first year is cheap, and you can 301 it or hold it parked. But the primary, linked-everywhere domain should be fox-agent.dev.

 

The notes file already recommends Phase 1 as an awesome-fox-agent GitHub repo with zero infrastructure — so you don't even need the domain live on day one. Buy it to park it, build the awesome repo first, and only stand up the registry service when volume justifies it.

 

Want me to update the notes file with this decision (.dev primary at Cloudflare, .app as optional insurance)?

Format confirmed working. Here's the fuller test picture, and the backslash result is the one real blocker.

 

The isolated finding: Bun 1.4.3's TOML parser fails on lone backslashes in double-quoted strings — v = "C:\\Users\\name" errors with "A Unicode escape must be followed by exactly 8 hex digits." It treats \U (from \Users) as a Unicode escape and chokes. Literal multibyte text, \t, \n, \" all work. So:

 

• Config values with Windows paths or regex (C:\Users\..., \d+, \.) — which fox-agent's config can legitimately hold on WSL — break Bun.TOML.parse.

• smol-toml handles these fine.

 

That's a genuine correctness gap for a config loader, not just an edge case. It would throw on real user configs.

 

Before I swap, the decisive test is the compiled binary — if bin/fox (built with bun build --compile) doesn't expose Bun.TOML, the whole thing is moot. Let me check that now, because it changes the recommendation:

 

• If Bun.TOML is in the compiled binary → we could swap, but I'd want to keep smol-toml for parse (to survive backslashes) and only use Bun.TOML.stringify. That's not a clean win.

• If it's not exposed → we keep smol-toml entirely.

 

Want me to run the compiled-binary check? And honestly, given the backslash bug, my recommendation is shifting to keep smol-toml — it's one tiny dep that handles the full TOML string spec correctly, and Bun's parser isn't a drop-in for config files that might contain Windows paths or regex. The swap saves ~1 dependency but buys a real parsing bug.

 

How do you want to proceed — still push the swap (with smol-toml retained for parse), or keep smol-toml?
