Format and todos fully live, ctx fix clearly working (ctx: 86783 is the estimate path). I've read the full wrap logic. Now I understand the missing-pipes bug precisely.

 

Root cause: the fence renderer emits ONE logical row [{t:"│ "}, ...codeSegs] per source line. The caller (app.ts) wraps that row at width-1. wrapSegs wraps at spaces — but a long code line with no spaces near the margin splits a word (the oversized-word branch, lines 80-95), and the continuation gets no gutter. Worse, wrapSegs splits at every space, so a code token containing spaces gets torn across rows unpredictably, and the │ prefix only survives on the first row.

 

The right fix: the fence renderer should emit its own continuation rows so every physical row carries the gutter. But renderMarkdown doesn't know the width — the caller does the wrapping. So I need the caller to add the gutter to code continuation rows. Let me look at how app.ts wraps these rows.

1: // MCP client bridge: connects configured stdio servers, merges their tools

2: // into the registry under mcp<server><tool>. The SDK is a dynamic import

3: // so fox-agent still runs (without MCP) if it isn't installed.

4: import type { McpServerConfig } from "../core/config.ts";

5: import type { MediaPart, ToolDef } from "../providers/types.ts";

6: import type { Tool, ToolResult } from "./types.ts";

7: import { fail, ok } from "./types.ts";

8: import { childEnv } from "../core/childenv.ts";

9: import { VERSION } from "../core/version.ts";

10:

11: const OUTCAPMCP = 30_000;

12:

13: /** Live clients, so shutdownTools() can reap the stdio children. */

14: interface LiveClient {

15: close: () => Promise<void>;

16: /** the stdio child's pid — closeMcp SIGKILLs it when a polite close hangs */

17: pid?: number;

18: }

19: let cache: { key: string; tools: Map<string, Tool>; warnings: string[]; clients: LiveClient[] } | null = null;

20:

21: /**

22: * MCP content parts -> ToolResult. Text joins as output; image parts become

23: * real MediaParts so a vision-capable model sees the picture instead of a

24: * JSON-stringified base64 blob (which is how chrome-devtools screenshots

25: * used to arrive — megabytes of base64 as plain text).

26: */

27: function toResult(content: unknown, isError: boolean): ToolResult {

28: const parts = content as { type?: string; text?: string; data?: string; mimeType?: string }[] | null;

29: if (!Array.isArray(parts)) {

30: const s = JSON.stringify(content ?? {});

31: return isError ? fail(s) : ok(s);

32: }

33: const text: string[] = [];

34: const media: MediaPart[] = [];

35: for (const p of parts) {

36: if (p?.type === "image" && typeof p.data === "string") {

37: media.push({ mimeType: p.mimeType ?? "image/png", data: p.data });

38: } else if (typeof p?.text === "string") {

39: text.push(p.text);

40: } else {

41: text.push(JSON.stringify(p));

42: }

43: }

44: const base = isError ? fail(text.join("\n").slice(0, OUTCAPMCP)) : ok(text.join("\n").slice(0, OUTCAPMCP));

45: return media.length ? { ...base, media } : base;

46: }

47:

48: export async function mcpTools(

49: servers: Record<string, McpServerConfig>,

50: ): Promise<{ tools: Map<string, Tool>; warnings: string[] }> {

51: const key = JSON.stringify(servers);

52: if (cache?.key === key) return { tools: cache.tools, warnings: cache.warnings };

53: // config changed — drop the old children before standing up new ones

54: // (fire-and-forget: the cache is cleared synchronously so the new pool

55: // builds fresh; the old children's SIGKILL reap runs in the background)

56: if (cache) closeMcp();

57:

58: const tools = new Map<string, Tool>();

59: const warnings: string[] = [];

60: const clients: LiveClient[] = [];

61:

62: for (const [name, cfg] of Object.entries(servers)) {

63: try {

64: const sdk = await import("@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js");

65: const stdio = await import("@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/stdio.js");

66: const client = new sdk.Client({ name: "fox-agent", version: VERSION });

67: const transport = new stdio.StdioClientTransport({

68: command: cfg.command,

69: args: cfg.args ?? [],

70: env: childEnv(cfg.env),

71: // SDK default is stderr inherit, which points at the parent's stderr —

72: // the TUI's own surface. A chatty server (npm exec wrappers print

73: // notices/warnings by the line) then smears garbage across the screen;

74: // its diagnostics are not worth the pixels, matching lsp/client.ts.

75: stderr: "ignore",

76: });

77: await client.connect(transport);

78: clients.push({ close: () => client.close(), pid: transport.pid ?? undefined });

79: const res = await client.listTools();

80: for (const t of res.tools) {

81: const def: ToolDef = {

82: name: mcp__${name}__${t.name},

83: description: [mcp:${name}] ${t.description ?? t.name},

84: parameters: (t.inputSchema as Record<string, unknown>) ?? { type: "object" },

85: };

86: tools.set(def.name, {

87: def,

88: run: async (args: any): Promise<ToolResult> => {

89: try {

90: const r = await client.callTool({ name: t.name, arguments: args });

91: return toResult(r.content, r.isError === true);

92: } catch (e) {

93: return fail(error: mcp call failed: ${(e as Error).message});

94: }

95: },

96: });

97: }

98: } catch (e) {

99: // every failing server is reported, not just the last one. console.error

100: // would smear the parent TUI (same reason server stderr is "ignore"

101: // above) — the warnings channel is what callers actually surface.

102: warnings.push(mcp server '${name}' unavailable: ${(e as Error).message.slice(0, 200)});

103: }

104: }

105:

106: cache = { key, tools, warnings, clients };

107: return { tools, warnings };

108: }

109:

110: /**

111: * Disconnect every live MCP client, killing their stdio children.

112: *

113: * Detached: the snapshot of live clients is taken and the cache cleared

114: * synchronously (so a follow-up session builds a fresh pool), but the actual

115: * close — and the SIGKILL safety net for a wedged child — runs in the

116: * background and is NOT awaited. Each close used to be raced against a 3s

117: * deadline inside the awaited shutdown path, so one hung server (measured: an

118: * npx chrome-devtools bridge over WSL interop whose close never settles)

119: * stalled the terminal handoff for the whole deadline even though the user

120: * had already been shown the resume hint. The polite window per server is

121: * unchanged; it now just overlaps process teardown instead of gating it.

122: */

123: export function closeMcp(): void {

124: const live = cache?.clients ?? [];

125: cache = null;

126: if (!live.length) return;

127: // fire-and-forget: callers must not await; the SIGKILL fallback in

128: // closeClients still reaps a child whose polite close hangs

129: void closeClients(live);

130: }

131:

132: /** The bounded close + SIGKILL fallback, exposed so tests can pin it.

133: *

134: * Runs detached from shutdown (closeMcp no longer awaits it), but stays

135: * bounded internally: a wedged client.close() that never settles must still

136: * yield to the SIGKILL within the polite window, or the background reaper

137: * would itself leak a hung promise and a live child.

138: */

139: const MCPCLOSETIMEOUTMS = 3000;

140: export async function closeClients(clients: LiveClient[]): Promise<void> {

141: await Promise.all(

142: clients.map(async (c) => {

143: try {

144: await Promise.race([c.close(), Bun.sleep(MCPCLOSETIMEOUT_MS)]);

145: } catch {}

146: // still alive after the polite window (close rejected, hung, or the

147: // promise settled while the child lingers) — the kill is unconditional:

148: // ESRCH for an already-dead pid is not an error state here

149: if (c.pid) {

150: try {

151: process.kill(c.pid, "SIGKILL");

152: } catch {}

153: }

154: }),

155: );

156: }

53: /**

54: * Full registry: built-ins + MCP servers + plugin tools, all from config.

55: * exclude names tools to drop; nothing in fox-agent uses it now that delegation is a

56: * separate process with its own full registry (src/tools/task.ts), and it is

57: * kept only as a general facility for an embedder that wants a reduced tool set.

58: * Note that a reduced registry is safe to build — buildSystemPrompt gates

59: * every tool-specific section on what is actually present — but it is no longer

60: * how subagents work.

61: *

62: * Returns MCP connection warnings, plugin load warnings and any config warnings

63: * so the caller can surface them all as warn at the top of the turn.

64: */

65: export async function buildRegistry(

66: cfg: Config,

67: exclude?: Set<string>,

68: ): Promise<{ tools: Map<string, Tool>; warnings: string[]; plugins: FoxPlugin[]; agents: Record<string, ExternalAgentConfig> }> {

70: setOutputCap(cfg.toolOutputCap ?? 30_000);

72: // by hand, and a config written before these fields existed must degrade to

78: // and delegation targets alongside its tools, and those merge before

79: // mcpTools dials out. Bundled plugins first, through the exact merge path

80: // user plugins take.

81: const { effectiveConfigPath } = await import("../core/config.ts");

82: const { dirname } = await import("node:path");

83: const res = await loadPlugins(cfg.plugins ?? [], dirname(effectiveConfigPath()), disabled);

84: warnings.push(...res.warnings);

85: const plugins: FoxPlugin[] = [

86: ...bundledPlugins().filter((p) => !bundledDisabled(p.name, disabled)),

87: ...bundledProviderPlugins(),

88: ...res.plugins,

206: describe("closeMcp: a wedged server must not hang shutdown", () => {

207: // The hang this pins: fox printed its resume hint and looked exited, but the

208: // process sat on closeMcp's unbounded Promise.all because one stdio server's

209: // client.close() never settles (measured with the npx chrome-devtools bridge

210: // over WSL interop). closeClients must return on its own and SIGKILL the child.

211: test("a close() that never settles returns within the deadline and kills the child", async () => {

212: const { closeClients } = await import("../src/tools/mcp.ts");

213: // a real live child, so the kill path is exercised against a real pid

214: const child = Bun.spawn(["sleep", "300"]);

215: let closeCalled = false;

216: const wedged = {

217: close: () =>

218: new Promise<void>(() => {

219: closeCalled = true; // never resolves

220: }),

221: pid: child.pid,

222: };

223: const t0 = Date.now();

224: await closeClients([wedged]);

225: const took = Date.now() - t0;

226: expect(closeCalled).toBe(true);

227: // bounded: the polite window, not forever (give the race a wide margin)

228: expect(took).toBeLessThan(10_000);

229: // the wedged server's child was force-killed, not left behind

230: await Bun.sleep(100); // signal delivery

231: const alive = Bun.spawnSync(["kill", "-0", String(child.pid)]).exitCode === 0;

232: expect(alive).toBe(false);

233: }, 30_000);

240: close: async () => {

241: await Bun.sleep(50);

242: resolved = true;

243: },

244: pid: child.pid,

245: };

246: await closeClients([good]);

247: expect(resolved).toBe(true);

248: // close() settled before the deadline; the pid was already gone or just

250: // is async, so give the kernel a beat before probing liveness.

251: await Bun.sleep(100);

252: const alive = Bun.spawnSync(["kill", "-0", String(child.pid)]).exitCode === 0;

253: expect(alive).toBe(false);

254: });

function promptClick(x: number, y: number) {

void x;

const p = prompt!;

const opts = promptOptions();

if (!opts.length) return;

// same geometry the menu paints with (see dockFloats) — anything else

// resolves clicks against rows the menu never occupied

const menuTop = dockFloats().top;

const MAX = Math.max(1, Math.min(5, menuTop - 1));

const start = opts.length <= MAX ? 0 : Math.max(0, Math.min(p.sel - Math.floor(MAX / 2), opts.length - MAX));

const end = Math.min(opts.length, start + MAX);

const above = start > 0 ? 1 : 0;

const below = end < opts.length ? 1 : 0;

const rows = 1 + above + (end - start) + below;

const idx = y - (menuTop - rows);

if (idx <= 0 || idx >= rows) return; // header, or outside the menu

const optRow = idx - 1 - above;

if (optRow < 0) {

p.sel = Math.max(0, p.sel - MAX); // "… above": page the highlight up

markDirty();

return;

}

if (optRow >= end - start) {

p.sel = Math.min(opts.length - 1, p.sel + MAX); // "… below": page down

markDirty();

return;

}

const i = start + optRow;

if (i === p.sel) promptSubmit(); // second click on the row confirms it

else {

p.sel = i;

markDirty();

}

}

 

function promptSubmit() {

const next = nextLiveStep(p.idx + 1, 1);

if (next < p.steps.length) {

p.idx = next;

enterPromptStep();

} else {

finishPrompt(p.answers);

}

}

function dockFloats(): { queueH: number; cmdH: number; top: number } {

const { inputTop } = dockGeom();

// painted frame's stack height when one is up (hit-tests match pixels)

const queueH = painted ? painted.queueH : queueStackH();

const cAvail = cmdOut?.length ? Math.max(1, inputTop - queueH - 1) : 0;

const cmdH = cmdOut?.length ? Math.min(cmdOut.length, cAvail) + (cmdOut.length > cAvail ? 1 : 0) : 0;

return { queueH, cmdH, top: inputTop - queueH - cmdH };

}

 

/**

* First screen row belonging to the dock: the queued/steering rows stacked

* above the input box plus the box itself. Same row budget paint() and

* onClick() use, so scroll routing agrees with the pixels about where the

* dock starts — the flex height and queue length fall out of dockGeom, no

* special case needed for either.

*/

function dockTopY(): number {

const { inputTop } = dockGeom();

return inputTop - (painted ? painted.queueH : queueStackH());

}

 

/** Height of the queued/steering stack, exactly as viewportH reserves it. */

function queueStackH(): number {

const pend = pendingLines();

if (!pend.length) return 0;

const { inputTop } = dockGeom();

const shown = pend.slice(0, Math.max(1, inputTop - 1)).length;

return shown + (pend.length > shown ? 1 : 0);

}

1: /**

2: * Delegation: a subagent is a real agent reached over a real protocol.

3: *

4: * A subagent used to be an in-process child session with a deliberately reduced

5: * tool registry. It is now a separate agent — by default another fox --acp

6: * child with the full registry, and optionally any agent the user named in

7: * fox-agent.toml under [agents.<name>]. The protocol follows the entry's

8: * shape: command spawns a child and speaks ACP, url reaches a running agent

9: * over HTTP and speaks A2A. There is no second code path left for "subagent":

10: * a child is a real session in a real process (or a real service), reached

11: * through the same protocols external tools use, so anything fox-agent can do

12: * for a user it can do for its parent.

13: *

14: * The visible upgrade on ACP: the child's updates stream into the parent's

15: * event stream as they happen, so the TUI shows the subagent's tool calls live

16: * instead of nothing until it finishes. A2A agents that implement

17: * message/stream (SSE) report state transitions the same way; servers

18: * without it fall back to polling and only the final report arrives.

19: */

20: import { existsSync } from "node:fs";

21: import { kvGet, kvSet } from "../store/db.ts";

22: import type { ToolDef } from "../providers/types.ts";

23: import type { ExternalAgentConfig } from "../core/config.ts";

24: import type { ToolContext, ToolResult } from "./types.ts";

25: import { fail, ok } from "./types.ts";

26:

27: /**

28: * How deep delegation may nest.

29: *

30: * The child is a full fox-agent with task in its registry, so without a cap a

31: * subagent can spawn a subagent forever — each one a real process burning real

32: * requests. The depth travels in the child's environment rather than a closure,

33: * because a closure cannot cross a process boundary.

34: */

35: const MAX_DEPTH = 3;

36: const DEPTHENV = "FOXAGENTDELEGATIONDEPTH";

37: // Malware/loop safety, not a capability cut: the agent keeps full delegation,

38: // but one session cannot fork-bomb the machine or pin gigabytes of reports.

39: const MAXBGTASKSPERSESSION = 8;

40: const MAXTASKRESULT = 50_000;

41:

42: export const taskDef: ToolDef = {

43: name: "task",

44: description:

45: "Delegate a self-contained subtask to a subagent: a separate agent with its own context window and session — a spawned child process spoken to over ACP, or a remote agent at a configured url spoken to over A2A. It has the same full tool access you do and cannot see this conversation, so give it complete standalone instructions. Returns its final report. With background:true the task starts detached and you get a job id back immediately — poll with task({job}) for status/result.",

46: parameters: {

47: type: "object",

48: properties: {

49: description: { type: "string", description: "One-line label shown in the UI" },

50: prompt: { type: "string", description: "Complete, standalone instructions for the subagent" },

51: agent: {

52: type: "string",

53: description: 'Which agent to delegate to: "default" (another fox-agent) or a name configured in fox-agent.toml [agents.*] (an ACP command or an A2A url)',

54: },

55: background: { type: "boolean", description: "Start detached; returns a job id immediately. Poll with task({job})." },

56: job: { type: "string", description: "Poll a background task: status while running, final report when done" },

57: },

58: required: [],

59: },

60: };

61:

62: /**

63: * How to re-launch this fox-agent as an ACP server.

64: *

65: * Compiled and from-source runs need opposite halves of the same pair. In a

66: * bun build --compile binary process.execPath IS fox-agent and Bun.main is a

67: * virtual /$bunfs/root/... path that no process can execute; running from

68: * source it is the other way around — execPath is bun and Bun.main is

69: * src/cli.ts. Probed both, rather than assumed.

70: */

71: export function selfAgent(): ExternalAgentConfig {

72: const main = Bun.main;

73: const compiled = main.startsWith("/$bunfs/") || !existsSync(main);

74: return compiled ? { command: process.execPath, args: ["--acp"] } : { command: process.execPath, args: [main, "--acp"] };

75: }

76:

77: function resolveAgent(name: string | undefined, agents: Record<string, ExternalAgentConfig>): ExternalAgentConfig | string {

78: if (!name || name === "default") return selfAgent();

79: const hit = agents[name];

80: if (hit) return hit;

81: const known = ["default", ...Object.keys(agents)].join(", ");

82: return error: unknown agent "${name}" — configure it in fox-agent.toml under [agents.${name}], or use one of: ${known};

83: }

84:

85: // ---- background tasks ------------------------------------------------------

86:

87: interface TaskJob {

88: id: string;

89: label: string;

90: startedAt: number;

91: done: boolean;

92: ok: boolean;

93: result: string;

94: ac: AbortController;

95: }

96:

97: const taskJobs = new Map<string, Map<string, TaskJob>>(); // sessionId -> id -> job

98: let taskSeq = 0;

99:

100: function sessionTasks(sessionId: string): Map<string, TaskJob> {

101: let m = taskJobs.get(sessionId);

102: if (!m) taskJobs.set(sessionId, (m = new Map()));

103: return m;

104: }

105:

106: function pollTask(args: { job: string }, ctx: ToolContext): ToolResult {

107: const job = sessionTasks(ctx.sessionId).get(args.job);

108: if (!job) return fail(error: no task ${args.job} in this session);

109: const secs = Math.floor((Date.now() - job.startedAt) / 1000);

110: if (!job.done) return ok(task ${job.id} (${job.label}) still running (${secs}s) — poll again with task({job:"${job.id}"}));

111: sessionTasks(ctx.sessionId).delete(args.job); // a settled task reaps on first read

112: const head = task ${job.id} (${job.label}) ${job.ok ? "finished" : "failed"} after ${secs}s;

113: const body = job.result.length > MAXTASKRESULT ? ${job.result.slice(-MAX_TASK_RESULT)}\n… (head truncated) : job.result;

114: return job.ok ? ok(${head}\n${body}) : fail(${head}\n${body});

115: }

116:

117: /** Session end: abort every detached subagent it started. */

118: export function killTasks(sessionId: string): void {

119: const m = taskJobs.get(sessionId);

120: if (!m) return;

121: for (const j of m.values()) if (!j.done) j.ac.abort();

122: taskJobs.delete(sessionId);

123: }

124:

125: export async function taskRun(

126: args: { description?: string; prompt?: string; agent?: string; background?: boolean; job?: string },

127: ctx: ToolContext,

128: ): Promise<ToolResult> {

129: if (args.job) return pollTask({ job: args.job }, ctx);

130: if (!args.prompt?.trim()) return fail("error: task needs prompt");

131: if (!args.description?.trim()) return fail("error: task needs description");

132:

133: if (args.background) {

134: const live = [...sessionTasks(ctx.sessionId).values()].filter((j) => !j.done).length;

135: if (live >= MAXBGTASKSPERSESSION) {

136: return fail(error: too many background tasks in this session (${live}/${MAX_BG_TASKS_PER_SESSION}) — poll one with task({job}) before starting more);

137: }

138: const id = t${++taskSeq};

139: const ac = new AbortController();

140: const job: TaskJob = { id, label: args.description.trim(), startedAt: Date.now(), done: false, ok: false, result: "", ac };

141: sessionTasks(ctx.sessionId).set(id, job);

142: // an aborted-by-session-end run rejects or cancels; both land in result

143: const sub = ac.signal.aborted ? ac.signal : (() => {

144: // link the caller's abort to the job's own controller

145: ctx.signal?.addEventListener("abort", () => ac.abort(), { once: true });

146: return ac.signal;

147: })();

148: void executeTask(args, { ...ctx, signal: sub })

149: .then((r) => {

150: job.done = true;

151: job.ok = r.ok;

152: job.result = r.output.length > MAXTASKRESULT ? r.output.slice(-MAXTASKRESULT) : r.output;

153: })

154: .catch((e) => {

155: job.done = true;

156: job.ok = false;

157: job.result = error: ${(e as Error).message ?? e}.slice(-MAXTASKRESULT);

158: });

159: return ok(task ${id} started in background (${job.label}) — poll with task({job:"${id}"}));

160: }

161:

162: return executeTask(args, ctx);

163: }

164:

165: async function executeTask(

166: args: { description?: string; prompt?: string; agent?: string },

167: ctx: ToolContext,

168: ): Promise<ToolResult> {

169:

170: const depth = Number(process.env[DEPTH_ENV] ?? 0) || 0;

171: if (depth >= MAXDEPTH) return fail(`error: delegation depth limit (${MAXDEPTH}) reached — do this subtask yourself`);

172:

173: const spec = resolveAgent(args.agent, ctx.agents ?? {});

174: if (typeof spec === "string") return fail(spec);

175:

176: const children = kvGet<string[]>(ctx.sessionId, "children") ?? [];

177: const label = args.description!.trim();

178: try {

179: // A2A: the entry points at a running agent over HTTP. Streams when the

180: // server speaks message/stream (SSE), polls otherwise.

181: if (spec.url) {

182: const { runA2aAgent } = await import("../a2a/client.ts");

183: const TERMINAL = new Set(["completed", "failed", "canceled", "rejected", "input-required"]);

184: const text = (

185: await runA2aAgent(spec.url, args.prompt!, {

186: signal: ctx.signal,

187: headers: spec.headers,

188: // forward remote state transitions the way an ACP child's tool calls

189: // are forwarded — the TUI shows only completions, --json shows all

190: onEvent: ctx.emit

191: ? (ev) => {

192: if (!ev.state) return;

193: ctx.emit?.({ type: "child_tool", session: label, name: remote ${ev.state}, done: TERMINAL.has(ev.state), ok: ev.state !== "failed" });

194: }

195: : undefined,

196: })

197: ).trim();

198: return ok(text ? ${text}\n\n[a2a task on ${args.agent ?? spec.url}] : [a2a agent ${args.agent ?? spec.url} finished without a final message]);

199: }

200:

201: // ACP: spawn a child process and stream its tool activity into the parent's

202: // stream as it happens. Lazy-imported so the ACP SDK stays off TUI startup.

203: if (!spec.command) return fail(error: agent "${args.agent ?? "default"}" has neither command nor url — fix fox-agent.toml [agents.${args.agent}]);

204: const { runAcpAgent } = await import("../acp/client.ts");

205: // ACP sends the tool's name on tool_call and only the id on

206: // tool_call_update, so the name has to be remembered across the two. Without

207: // this the parent's UI reports raw call ids ("c1") for the child's work.

208: const names = new Map<string, string>();

209: const res = await runAcpAgent({

210: command: spec.command,

211: args: spec.args,

212: cwd: ctx.cwd,

213: prompt: args.prompt!,

214: signal: ctx.signal,

215: env: { ...spec.env, [DEPTH_ENV]: String(depth + 1) },

216: // Forward the child's tool activity into the parent's stream so its work is

217: // visible while it happens. Text is deliberately not forwarded: it is this

218: // tool's return value, and echoing it live would report it twice.

219: onUpdate: ctx.emit

220: ? (u) => {

221: if (u.sessionUpdate === "tool_call") {

222: const name = u.name ?? u.title;

223: names.set(u.toolCallId, name);

224: ctx.emit?.({ type: "child_tool", session: label, name, done: false, ok: true });

225: } else if (u.sessionUpdate === "toolcallupdate" && (u.status === "completed" || u.status === "failed")) {

226: ctx.emit?.({

227: type: "child_tool",

228: session: label,

229: name: names.get(u.toolCallId) ?? u.title ?? u.toolCallId,

230: done: true,

231: ok: u.status === "completed",

232: });

233: }

234: }

235: : undefined,

236: });

237:

238: kvSet(ctx.sessionId, "children", [...children, res.sessionId]);

239:

240: if (res.stopReason === "cancelled") return fail(error: subagent cancelled${res.text ? \n\n${res.text} : ""});

241: const text = res.text.trim();

242: return ok(text ? ${text}\n\n[subagent session ${res.sessionId}] : [subagent ${res.sessionId} finished without a final message]);

243: } catch (e) {

244: return fail(error: subagent failed: ${(e as Error).message});

245: }

246: }

1: /**

2: * The built-in tools that ship AS plugins. Same FoxPlugin shape a third-party

3: * module exports, loaded through the same merge path in buildRegistry, so:

4: *

5: * - a user plugin can shadow one of these by name (later registration wins,

6: * with a warning) exactly the way it shadows any other tool;

7: * - disabledPlugins = ["pty"] turns one off without touching code;

8: * - the pty plugin demonstrates the lifecycle seam: its tmux session is

9: * released from onSessionEnd, not from a special case in the harness.

10: * - the repl plugin demonstrates the same seam for lighter state: its

11: * per-session scratchpad is dropped from onSessionEnd.

12: */

13: import type { FoxPlugin } from "./types.ts";

14: import { ptyDef, drivePty, cleanupPty, ptySessionName } from "../tools/pty.ts";

15: import { todoDef, todoRun } from "../tools/todo.ts";

16: import { fetchDef, fetchRun } from "../tools/fetch.ts";

17: import { replDef, replRun, cleanupRepl } from "../tools/repl.ts";

18: import { questionPlugin } from "../tools/question.ts";

19: import { lspPlugin } from "../tools/lsp.ts";

20: import costPlugin, { costSegment } from "./cost.ts";

21:

22: const ptyPlugin: FoxPlugin = {

23: name: "bundled:pty",

24: tools: [{ def: ptyDef, run: drivePty }],

25: hooks: {

26: // tmux sessions outlive the fox-agent turn that made them; the hook is what

27: // ties their lifetime to the session's, on exit AND on session switch

28: onSessionEnd: (c) => cleanupPty(ptySessionName(c.sessionId)),

29: },

30: };

31:

32: const todoPlugin: FoxPlugin = { name: "bundled:todo", tools: [{ def: todoDef, run: todoRun }] };

33: const fetchPlugin: FoxPlugin = { name: "bundled:fetch", tools: [{ def: fetchDef, run: fetchRun }] };

34:

35: const replPlugin: FoxPlugin = {

36: name: "bundled:repl",

37: tools: [{ def: replDef, run: replRun }],

38: hooks: {

39: // the scratchpad is per-session memory; drop it with the session

40: onSessionEnd: (c) => cleanupRepl(c.sessionId),

41: },

42: };

43:

44: /** All bundled plugins. Order matters only for shadowing: user plugins load after. */

45: export function bundledPlugins(): FoxPlugin[] {

46: return [ptyPlugin, todoPlugin, fetchPlugin, replPlugin, questionPlugin, lspPlugin, costPlugin];

47: }

48:

49: /**

50: * The cost plugin's TUI segment. Lives beside the plugin (not inside it)

51: * because plugin statusSegments resolve without session context; the TUI

52: * calls this per frame with the active session. disabledPlugins keeps it

53: * consistent: disabling bundled:cost removes the tally everywhere.

54: */

55: export { costSegment };

56:

57: /**

58: * Does a disabledPlugins entry name this bundled plugin? Accepts "pty" and

59: * "bundled:pty" alike — the prefix is our namespacing, not the user's problem.

60: */

61: export function bundledDisabled(name: string, disabled: string[]): boolean {

62: const short = name.replace(/^bundled:/, "");

63: return disabled.some((d) => d === name || d === short);

64: }

1: # fox-agent — roadmap & decisions

2:

3: fox-agent (fox) — light coding harness with agent-controlled context. Built to be used for building itself (dogfooding).

4: Repo: github.com/QQSHI13/fox-agent · local ~/.openclaw/workspace/projects/fox-agent · binary bin/fox (+ sidecar libopentui.so) · npm fox-agent

5:

6: ## Identity

7: - Name: foxc → renamed fox-agent (npm blocked "foxc" as too similar to solc; CLI is fox) (npm/PyPI/brew free at planning time; GitHub user taken = irrelevant)

8: - Avoided trademark traps: qodex (~Codex), foxcode/openfox (taken), clawd-style near-misses

9:

10: ## Locked design decisions

11: | Area | Decision |

12: |---|---|

13: | Language | TypeScript on Bun (one language core→TUI→plugins→future web) |

14: | Core | ~80-line agent loop; everything else = tools/hooks |

15: | Tools v1 | read, write, edit, glob, grep, exec (one-shot + persistent pty via tmux), ctx_edit |

16: | Context | inline [mN] markers on every message; NO history_list tool — LLM sees IDs natively |

17: | ctx_edit | batched delete(+summary placeholder)/replace ops; view-only, storage immutable |

18: | Sessions | SQLite WAL, INSERT-only message DAG (parent_id), refs table (branches/reverts), ops table (view surgery events), failures logged as rows |

19: | Permissions | NONE — pi-style full control; env passthrough |

20: | Providers | tokenguard gateway first (one URL+key, OpenAI-compatible); thin Provider port for direct mode |

21: | Runtime header | cwd/git/os/date/model/version injected per prompt build, moved to BOTTOM of system prompt |

22: | UI | wrapper-first TUI on @opentui/solid (user rejected linear-stream: needs owned viewport for history rewrite + tty-without-scrollback) |

23:

24: ## Roadmap

25: - v1 — DONE: agent loop · tools (read/write/edit/glob/grep/exec/pty/ctx_edit/todowrite/task/fetch) · SQLite sessions+refs+ops · runtime header · streaming OpenAI-compatible provider · TUI · slash commands · ! shell mode · \ escape syntax · MCP client (live-tested 2026-08 against a real stdio server, test/mcp.test.ts)

26: - v1.5 — DONE: Plugin API — src/plugins/, one module registers tools + lifecycle hooks (onSessionStart/beforeLLMCall/afterTool) + custom providers

27: - v2 — DONE: ACP server (fox --acp) · ACP client (what task is built on) · LSP integration (diagnostics, TS/Python/Rust built in). Closed 2026-08 by scripts/acp-accept.ts, an acceptance check driving the compiled binary with the real external acpx client.

28: - v3 (next, deferred): A2A delegation · OpenAI-compatible endpoint (serve fox-agent as a model) · web UI

29:

30: Roadmap history: originally ACP-first; reordered wrapper-first because history rewrite is the core feature and terminals have scroll limits. v1.5 was skipped past at the time and picked back up after v2 closed.

31:

32: ## Plugin trust decision (do not reopen)

33: Plugins load from ~/.config/fox/config.toml only. A plugins key in a project fox.toml is ignored with

34: a warning naming both files. Reason: every other extension point ([mcpServers.*], [agents.*], [lsp.*])

35: spawns a child through childEnv(), which strips *_API_KEY/FOX_AUTH*. A plugin cannot be sandboxed that

36: way — it is imported into fox's own process and inherits the whole environment, API key included. So

37: "clone a repo, cd in, run fox" must not execute that repo's code. This is why applyTable takes a

38: scope: "global" | "project" parameter, which it needs for exactly this one key, and why Config grew a

39: warnings: string[] (there had to be somewhere to put the message — silence is the one outcome you cannot

40: debug). Verified against the compiled binary, not just a unit test.

41:

42: Hooks are patch-based and additive. beforeLLMCall returns {appendSystem?}, afterTool returns

43: {output?}. Neither can reorder or drop messages, so renderContext's invariant (every assistant

44: tool_call followed by its tool_result) holds by construction — a hook returning a message array would

45: hand that invariant to plugin authors, and breaking it surfaces as a provider 400 that names nothing.

46: afterTool runs between execToolCall and appendMessage, so the patched text is the only version stored,

47: shown to the model, and reported via tool_end.

48:

49: ## Hard-won technical facts (do not relearn these)

50: - Bun's JSX transform is react-style → must build with @opentui/solid/bun-plugin (babel-preset-solid) or nothing reactive works; opencode uses vite for the same reason

51: - Compiled binary + FFI: ship libopentui.so beside binary and call setRenderLibPath() before renderer creation (two-step build: bundle w/ plugin → bun build --compile dist/cli.js)

52: - Mark other-platform @opentui/core-* natives as external in Bun.build

53: - OpenAI wire format: toolcalls must nest {id,type:"function",function:{name,arguments}}; every toolcall needs a following tool msg (pairing repair needed after surgery)

54: - Deleting tool results requires hiding parent assistant's tool_call too (orphan repair in context renderer)

55: - clipboardy/execa crashes bun-compiled binaries → OSC52 + powershell/wl-copy/xclip spawners instead

56: - opentui textarea won't take focus reliably → custom input on global useKeyboard; exitOnCtrlC must be disabled for smart ctrl+c

57: - zen gateway streams reasoning_content deltas (thinking)

58: - acpx --json-strict does not police the agent. It suppresses acpx's own non-JSON stderr. acpx's stdout under --format json is acpx's reconstruction of the conversation, and its ndjson reader silently skips an agent line it cannot parse — so a stray console.log in fox's ACP server is invisible from acpx's output. Stdout purity can only be proved by a direct spawn-and-read of fox's own stdout. Found by sabotage: a console.log in runAcpServer left all checks green.

59: - acpx needs the exec subcommand; a bare prompt exits 4 NO_SESSION because it wants a pre-existing acpx-managed session record.

60: - In-process protocol tests share assumptions. All 31 ACP tests use client().connectWith(buildAgent(...)) — same SDK objects on both ends, so a wrong field name or a mishandled advertised capability passes every one. Only a foreign client proves the wire format.

61: - Bun's module registry caches a dynamically imported plugin and resetPlugins() cannot clear it. Anything a plugin reads from process.env at module scope freezes to the first caller's value — read it per call.

62: - A compiled binary cannot load a plugin that imports from src/. A plugin fixture used with bin/fox must depend only on node builtins (or the published package), which is also the position a real user's plugin is in.

63:

66: Core rewrite landed: layout (core/store/context/loop/providers/tools), turn manager (step cap, retries, parallel tools, abort-safe partials), auto-compaction via ops, pairing-repair in projection, append-only undo, forks, config cascade (.fox.json + AGENTS.md), anthropic provider w/ caching, MCP client bridge, headless -p/--json, sdk.ts createAgent. 100: ## Deferred: Anthropic cache TTL — decided 2026-10-04, deliberately NOT in this round

101:

102: Skip ttl: "1h" for now and measure first: the cached_tokens plumbing (hit rate in /usage and in

103: the status bar) lands in this round, and the TTL call gets made against a real hit rate rather than

104: against arithmetic alone. Do not quietly fold the TTL change into that commit.

105:

106: What was established — don't re-derive it:

107:

108: - Mixed TTLs are legal, but ordered: a longer-TTL breakpoint must come BEFORE a shorter one. Two

109: independent sources agree — an API FAQ ("Yes, but with constraints. Longer TTL breakpoints must come

110: before shorter ones.") and agno's docs, which call a 5m block preceding a 1h block a violation of

111: "Anthropic's mixed-TTL ordering rule". src/providers/anthropic.ts marks rest[len-2] (stable) and

112: rest[len-1] (runtime tail), i.e. the earlier index first, so 1h → 5m is the legal order and every

113: candidate shape below is valid.

114: - Pricing: 5m write 1.25x, 1h write 2x, read 0.1x either way. The TTL refreshes free on every hit, so

115: an active turn never expires it — only an idle gap does, and those live at turn boundaries (a human

116: reading a diff for six minutes). Break-even: one avoided re-write per hour covers the 2x premium

117: (0.75P paid once, ~0.9P saved per avoided re-write at prompt size P).

118: - Today's two breakpoints are not equivalent. rest[len-1] is the ephemeral runtime tail, rewritten

119: every step, so that entry is never read — it is a pure 1.25x write. rest[len-2] is the last stable

120: history message, the one every subsequent step actually reads. Candidate shapes, cheapest first:

121: stable 1h + tail left at 5m (legal, minimal) / both 1h (no mixing, tail write goes to 2x) / drop the

122: tail breakpoint entirely and put 1h on the stable one alone (optimal; needs a length guard, and no

123: production caller lacks a tail).

124: - OpenCode (~/opencode-v2) ships none of it: packages/ai/src/cache-policy.ts, default policy

125: "auto" = last tool + first and last system parts + conversation tail, capped at 4 breakpoints (the

126: Anthropic API 400s past that). No ttl on the wire by default — ttlBucket() only emits "1h" when

127: ttlSeconds >= 3600 — and there is no user config surface for the knob. It does capture

128: cacheReadInputTokens/cacheWriteInputTokens into tokens.cache.{read,write}, aggregates and costs

129: them, but shows no hit rate anywhere in its UI.

130:

131: ## opencode study (2026-10-07)

132: Sources: opencode.ai/docs/{intro,providers,zen,share,agents,tools,tui,lsp}, repo (now anomalyco/opencode)

133: source via GitHub contents API: packages/opencode/src/plugin/openai/codex.ts,

134: packages/core/src/github-copilot/, packages/web/src/content/docs/{providers,tools,zen}.mdx.

135: Note: repo moved from sst/opencode to anomalyco/opencode ("© Anomaly"); raw.githubusercontent.com blocked

136: from this box — use curl -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" https://api.github.com/repos/....

137:

138: ### 1. Quota / usage display

139: - No documented /usage command in v2 TUI (command list: connect, compact, details, editor, export,

140: init, models, new, redo, sessions, share, themes, thinking, undo, unshare). Usage surfaces live in

141: the status/context area + provider dashboards; docs are thin here.

142: - OpenCode Zen: pay-per-request credits, auto-reload when balance drops below $5, and workspace-level

143: AND per-member monthly usage limits ("set a monthly usage limit to $20, Zen will not use more than

144: $20 in a month"). OpenCode Go = low-cost subscription plan. Deprecated-models table per provider.

145: - Context management is a hidden compaction agent (primary mode, not selectable) that auto-compacts

146: long context; users can also /compact (alias /summarize).

147: - fox-agent shows ctx N% (xk/yk) · cache N% but has no per-message/session cost estimate, no provider

148: plan-limit/quota display, and no remaining-until-compact indicator.

149: → fox-agent: add a cost-per-session estimate + provider quota line to the status bar; auto-compact threshold is the more valuable steal.

150:

151: ### 2. ChatGPT subscription without an API key (Codex)

152: From codex.ts — it's OAuth 2.0 + PKCE against OpenAI's auth issuer, NOT an API key:

153: - issuer https://auth.openai.com, clientid `appEMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann` (Codex CLI's client id)

154: - authorize URL params: response_type=code, scope="openid profile email offline_access",

155: code_challenge_method=S256, codex_cli_simplified_flow=true, originator=opencode

156: - redirect: opencode spins a local HTTP server on port 1455 and serves an OAuth callback page

157: - token exchange + refresh: POST {issuer}/oauth/token with PKCE verifier / refresh_token grant

158: - inference goes to https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses (Responses API), chatgptaccountid

159: extracted from id_token JWT claims (chatgpt_account_id or https://api.openai.com/auth)

160: - stored in ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json (chmod 0600) as `{type:"oauth", refresh, access,

161: expires, accountId}; auth store also supports {type:"api", key} and {type:"wellknown"}`;

162: OPENCODE_AUTH_CONTENT env can inject the whole auth JSON

163: - client-side model allowlist (gpt-5.x set) with gpt-5.5-pro explicitly disallowed

164: → fox-agent: replicable in ~100 lines — loopback listener + PKCE S256 + refresh persisted 0600; same pattern works for any OAuth-native subscription backend.

165:

166: ### 3. GitHub Copilot support

167: - /connect → "GitHub Copilot" → standard GitHub OAuth device flow: opens

168: github.com/login/device, user enters code like 8F43-6FCF, TUI polls until authorized.

169: - Stored as the oauth auth record (supports enterpriseUrl for GHES). Models are then picked via

170: /models; some need a Copilot Pro+ plan.

171: - Transport: a vendored in-repo openai-compatible AI SDK provider

172: (packages/core/src/github-copilot/ with chat + responses paths) pointing at Copilot's endpoints.

173: → fox-agent: GitHub device flow + a thin openai-compatible provider shim = Copilot support; reuse for GHES.

174:

175: ### 4. Web search / fetch tools

176: - webfetch: built-in, permission-gated ("fetch and read web pages").

177: - websearch: exists but gated — only when using the OpenCode/OpenCode Go provider, or when

178: OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA=1 / OPENCODE_ENABLE_PARALLEL=1. Backend is Exa or Parallel's hosted MCP

179: service, "no API key is required". Docs tip: websearch = discovery, webfetch = retrieval.

180: - No native provider web_search tool integration (unlike Claude API's server-side search).

181: → fox-agent: ship a search tool env-gated the same way; the hosted-MCP-no-key trick only works with their own backend, so ours would need Exa/Brave keys.

182:

183: ### 5. LSP integration

184: - Off by default. lsp: true enables all built-ins, lsp: {} keeps built-ins + add overrides.

185: - ~35 built-in servers keyed by file extension (typescript, pyright, rust-analyzer, gopls, eslint,

186: vue, svelte, yaml...); some auto-install (astro, terraform, yaml, kotlin, lua, php); others need the

187: toolchain on PATH. OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD=true blocks auto-download.

188: - On file open: match extension → start server if not running. **Diagnostics are fed back to the

189: agent as feedback.**

190: - Config shape: `lsp: { "<name>": { disabled?, command: string[], extensions: string[], env?,

191: initialization? } }` (initialization = server-specific init options, e.g. intelephense prefs).

192: - Experimental lsp tool (OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_LSP_TOOL=true) exposes goToDefinition,

193: findReferences, hover, documentSymbol, workspaceSymbol, goToImplementation, call hierarchy.

194: - Honest best-practices note in docs: LSP often isn't a net positive (drift, memory, version skew);

195: letting the agent run lint/typecheck CLIs is frequently better — enable only when it helps.

196: → fox-agent: we already feed diagnostics (v2, TS/Python/Rust); steal the on-demand lsp navigation tool behind an env flag + the opt-in default-off stance.

197:

198: ### 6. Share / link feature

199: - /share creates opncd.ai/s/<share-id>: unique public URL, conversation history + metadata synced

200: to their servers, link copied to clipboard. /unshare deletes it.

201: - Config share: "manual" (default) | "auto" (every new session shared) | "disabled"

202: (project-checked-in opencode.json enforces it for a team).

203: - Enterprise: disable entirely, restrict to SSO users, or self-host.

204: - Data retention: stays public until explicitly unshared.

205: → fox-agent: nice-to-have only; if built, manual-by-default + disabled mode + export-to-markdown (they also have /export) covers most of the value.

206:

207: ### 7. Multi-agent per project

208: - Primary agents (you talk to them; Tab cycles): built-in Build (all tools) and Plan (edits+bash

209: permission-denied). Subagents (invoked by primaries per description, or manually @mentioned):

210: General (full tools, parallel work units), Explore (read-only codebase), Scout (read-only, clones

211: dependency repos into a managed cache for upstream comparison).

212: - Hidden system agents (mode primary, hidden: true, not selectable): compaction, title (session

213: titles), summary (session summaries) — all automatic.

214: - Definition: JSON agent.<name> in opencode.json or markdown+frontmatter in `~/.config/opencode/

215: agents/ (global) and .opencode/agents/` (project); filename = agent name. Frontmatter:

216: description (required), mode, model (anthropic/claude-...), prompt ({file:./prompts/x.txt}

217: include syntax), temperature, topP, max steps/tokens, permission, color, hidden.

218: - Child sessions: subagent work becomes navigable child sessions (keybinds sessionchildfirst /

219: sessionchildcycle / session_parent).

220: → fox-agent: our task/ACP subagents cover dispatch; steal (a) markdown-defined project agents with per-agent model+permission, (b) the hidden-system-agent pattern for title/summary/compaction.

221:

222: ### 8. Other v2-era odds worth eyeing (short)

223: - Permissions model: allow|ask|deny per tool + wildcards ("mymcp_*": "ask"), overridable per

224: agent; Plan agent is just permission config. (fox-agent is deliberately permission-free — note as

225: the escape hatch for a future paranoid mode, not a default.)

226: - /undo + /redo: restores conversation AND file changes, implemented via git snapshotting

227: (requires project be a git repo).

228: - question tool: model asks the user structured questions mid-run.

229: - apply_patch tool: accepts multi-file patch text (Add/Update/Move/Delete markers) — codex-style.

230: - Skills: skill tool loads SKILL.md files into context (ClawHub-compatible shape).

231: - TUI ergonomics: ctrl+x leader key; /details toggle tool output; /thinking toggle; @file

232: fuzzy refs; ! bash; /editor composes in $EDITOR; /export to markdown; session title/summary

233: auto-generated by hidden agents.

234: - Models.dev: shared provider/model metadata registry (75+ providers) — config blacklist/

235: whitelist per provider to prune the /models picker.

236: - Zen "Jev": a "System One" endpoint that answers typed yes/no/choice/score questions instead of

237: generating text — cheap model-as-verifier for agent control flow.

238: - SDK + headless server + web UI + ACP support + IDE extensions; plugins from global config only.

239: → fox-agent: top three cheap steals: git-backed /undo//redo, the hidden title/summary agents, and the question tool.

240:

241: ## Self-documentation research (2026-10-07) — pi + opencode-v2

242:

243: ### pi (github.com/earendil-works/pi, packages/coding-agent)

244: - Docs ship INSIDE the package: getPackageDir()/docs/*.md (~25 files: extensions, themes, keybindings, skills, sdk, tui, models, mcp, custom-provider...) + README + examples/. getPackageDir() = env PI_PACKAGE_DIR override, else resolved from the compiled binary path.

245: - The ONLY mechanism is a system-prompt routing section (system-prompt.ts ~162): "Pi documentation (read only when the user asks about pi itself...)" with a topic→file map (extensions → docs/extensions.md, themes → docs/themes.md, ...), plus rules: read docs completely, follow .md cross-references, resolve docs/... under the docs path not cwd.

246: - No special tool. The agent uses its ordinary read tool on real files. Skills do progressive disclosure the same way: name+description in prompt, SKILL.md read on demand.

247:

248: ### opencode-v2 (~/opencode-v2)

249: - /init = a PROMPT TEMPLATE, not a tool: packages/core/src/plugin/command/initialize.txt (65 lines) injected as a user turn via the command plugin. Content: "Create or update AGENTS.md... every line should answer 'would an agent miss this without help?'... read highest-value sources first (README, manifests, build config, CI, existing instruction files)... prefer executable sources of truth over prose... only ask the user what the repo cannot answer... if AGENTS.md exists, improve in place — preserve verified guidance, delete fluff."

250: - Config self-edit: NO dedicated tool, NO system-prompt mention. The agent edits opencode.json with ordinary file tools; config discovery/validation picks it up. (pi same: config via docs + ordinary tools.)

251:

252: ### → fox-agent design (decided)

253: - fox compiles to ONE binary — no package dir to read docs from. So: author docs as .md files under docs/agent/ in the repo, EMBED them at build time (bun text imports), MATERIALIZE to agentHome()/docs/ at startup (version-stamped dir, rewrite when version changes) so the agent's read tool sees real paths.

254: - buildSystemPrompt gains a "Self documentation" section (pi-style routing): "read only when the user asks about fox-agent itself" + topic→file map (config, plugins, tools, acp, themes, keybindings/TUI, sessions).

255: - /init slash command = opencode-style template (adapted: fox-agent.toml + AGENTS.md, mentions validate callbacks throw, global-only plugins) injected as a user turn via runAgent.

256: - Config self-edit needs nothing special — the agent already has write/edit + /reload exists. The docs routing section is what makes the agent KNOW it can.

257:

258: ## Domain + plugin market + session export/share (2026-10-08)

259:

260: ### Domain for a future plugin/extension market

261: - Recommendation: foxagent.dev (short, clean; .dev enforces HTTPS — good for a registry that

262: serves install manifests). Register also fox-agent.dev (people will type the dash; 301 it).

263: - Fallbacks in order: foxagent.sh (CLI-flavored), getfox.dev (the "get<pattern>"), foxagent.io if

264: .dev taken. Avoid .ai (expensive renewal, screams "wrapper").

265: - Architecture note: the market does NOT need the domain to be a hosted service on day one.

266: Phase 1: an awesome-fox-agent GitHub repo — curated TOML/JS plugin list with one-line

267: descriptions, categories, install = paste a path/URL into global config plugins.entries.

268: Zero infrastructure, review via PRs, the same way awesome-* lists and clawhub's early days work.

269: Phase 2: when volume justifies it, registry service on the domain (manifests + tarballs +

270: fox install <name>), and the awesome repo becomes the curated front page pointing at it.

271: - ClawHub precedent worth copying: slug-based install (clawhub install <slug>), but keep

272: fox-agent's rule that plugins load from GLOBAL config only (security boundary — the market

273: must never make project-local plugin loading look sanctioned).

274:

275: ### Session export/share design (how opencode/pi do it, and the fox shape)

276: - opencode: server-side share — opencode share uploads the session to their cloud, returns

277: a URL; sync data model with an explicit share object; /unshare revokes. Requires a server.

278: - pi: export-html package — LOCAL static HTML render of the session (template.html/css/js

279: in core/export-html, tool renderer hooks so plugins can render their own tool calls). No

280: server, no account; the file is yours to host anywhere. SessionManager entries → HTML.

281: - → fox-agent (decided shape): pi-style local export first, no service.

282: 1. /export exists already (markdown). Add /share = self-contained HTML file written to

283: cwd (or --out): session rendered with the TUI's own theme colors (getResolvedThemeColors

284: pattern), syntax-highlighted code blocks, tool calls collapsed/expandable (details/summary),

285: images inlined as data URIs. Static single file, no JS dependencies, works offline.

286: 2. Optional public path = user hosts the file themselves ( gist, S3, their site). No fox server,

287: no phone-home, nothing to trust. If a hosted share is ever wanted, it's a THIRD-PARTY plugin

288: (share-to-<service>) — the core never uploads transcripts anywhere (privacy rule).

289: 3. Implementation seam: the session store already has allMessagesLite(); an exporter walks

290: items → HTML via a small renderer; reuse the markdown/highlight code from the TUI row

291: renderer where possible; a plugin-style renderer hook so bundled tool plugins can render

292: their calls/results (pi's ToolHtmlRenderer pattern).

294: ## Task log 2026-10-12 (user: qq, WSL2)

295:

296: ### Context accounting fix (the kimi under-report bug) — DONE, committed

297: Session mv0ucgs0cd9d3caa grew to ~2.1M tokens while the status bar read ~6% and compaction never fired, until the provider rejected the request at its real 1M limit. Root cause: the provider (kimi-for-coding @ api.kimi.com/coding/v1) tokenizes loosely and its prompt_tokens badly under-reads the real on-wire prompt, and fox-agent trusted that report alone for the compaction trigger, the checkBudget nudge, and the ctx % status bar.

298:

299: Probed endpoint behavior (do not re-derive):

300: - Large unique prompt (20000 words ≈ 29227 by chars/4) → prompt_tokens: 20092 (~1 token/word, ~25% under chars/4).

301: - Same payload again (cache hit) → prompt_tokens: 20092, cached_tokens: 20092. So prompt_tokens is the TOTAL; cached_tokens is a subset flag, NOT a third bucket. Summing prompt + cached double-counts every cache hit.

302: - Small fully-cached prompt (88 tok) → prompt_tokens: 88, cached_tokens: 88 (looked like "uncached-only" but the large-prompt probe disproves that).

303:

304: Fix (84f34e1, rebased to f510d26): new sessionContextTokens(sessionId) in src/context/budget.ts returns max(lastPromptTokens, chars/4 estimate of the whole visible history). max, not report + delta, because both are totals of the same history. Wired into compactIfNeeded, checkBudget, and the TUI status bar. Extracted nodeTokenEstimate (content + [N] marker + framing + attachments + tool args) so the estimate matches what the renderer bills. Verified: 802 pass / 0 fail, tsc clean.

Root cause: src/tui/highlight.ts tints any capitalized identifier as a "type" and uses a cross-language KEYWORDS union that includes JS in/this, Rust Self, etc. Decision pending: minimal regex-patch vs a real grammar lib (Shiki/highlight.js). Open.

318:

319: ### Dependency list (package.json)

320: dependencies: @agentclientprotocol/sdk ^1.5.1 · @ai-sdk/anthropic ^4.0.69 · @ai-sdk/google ^4.0.86 · @ai-sdk/openai ^4.0.82 · @ai-sdk/openai-compatible ^3.0.60 · @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.31.0 · ai ^7.0.123 · smol-toml ^1.9.0

321: devDependencies: bun-types ^1.4.2 · typescript 5.9.3

322:

323: ## Bun TOML audit (2026-10-12) — KEEP smol-toml for now

324: smol-toml is used only in src/core/config.ts (parse at read, stringify at write). Tested Bun 1.4.3 native Bun.TOML as a replacement. Findings:

325: - parse: handles the fox config shape, nested arrays, multiline strings, datetimes (→ Temporal objects, not strings).

326: - stringify: present in 1.4.3 (was broken in 1.4.1), round-trips stably.

327: - BLOCKER: Bun's parser rejects lone backslashes in double-quoted strings (v = "C:\Users\name" → "A Unicode escape must be followed by exactly 8 hex digits"). It misparses \U/\d as Unicode escapes. Real fox configs can hold Windows paths / regex → would throw on load. smol-toml handles these correctly.

328: - Action: KEEP smol-toml. File a Bun issue for the backslash parser bug; revisit the swap once fixed. Also verify Bun.TOML is exposed in the compiled bun build --compile binary before any future swap.

329:

330: ## Domain decision (2026-10-12)

331: fox-agent.dev + foxagent.dev (no-dash) at Cloudflare, same price (~$12.20 first year, renews at cost). fox-agent.dev is canonical; foxagent.dev 301-redirects. Both cheap enough to own as typo insurance. .dev is HSTS-preloaded (HTTPS-only forever — fine for a registry, but means no plain-HTTP ever). fox-agent.app ($8.20 first yr / $14.20 renew) skipped — .dev is cheaper long-term and signals dev-tool.

332:

333: ## Provider usage-stats format (researched 2026-10-12)

334: How prompt/cached/completion tokens are reported, per provider family. fox-agent's StreamEvent.usage = { prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cached_tokens? }, normalized by the AI SDK so prompt_tokens is the billed TOTAL and cached_tokens is the subset read from cache.

335:

336: - OpenAI Chat Completions (kimi-for-coding's format): usage.prompt_tokens = total billed input INCLUDING cached; usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens = the cached subset; usage.completion_tokens; completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens (o1+). Key: prompt_tokens is a TOTAL, cached is a subset flag — never sum them.

337: - Anthropic Messages: input_tokens (total), output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens (read, cheap), cache_creation_input_tokens (WRITTEN this call, the 1.25x/2x premium). cache_read>0 = a hit; cache_creation = the write cost. Input = cacheread + cachecreation + uncached remainder, billed at 3 different rates.

338: - Google Gemini: promptTokenCount, candidatesTokenCount, totalTokenCount, cachedContentTokenCount (cached prefix), promptTokensDetails.modalityTokenCount[], cacheTokensDetails (2.5).

339:

340: The cost plugin (src/plugins/cost.ts) already reads models.dev cache_read/cache_write rates. The earlier under-report bug was kimi sending a garbage prompt_tokens, not the shape — the shape/normalization is correct.

341:

342: smol-toml → Bun.TOML swap DONE (2026-10-12): src/core/config.ts now uses Bun.TOML.parse/stringify; smol-toml dep removed; 25 config tests pass; tsc clean. (The backslash-escape GH issue #45036 still stands for the error-message wording, but is moot for fox-agent: Linux/macOS only, WSL reaches Windows via /mnt/c/... forward slashes, no backslash config values.)

{"content":"# fox-agent — roadmap, decisions & status\n\n**fox-agent** (`fox`) — light coding harness with **agent-controlled context**. Built to be used for building itself (dogfooding).\nRepo: github.com/QQSHI13/fox-agent · local `~/.openclaw/workspace/projects/fox-agent` · binary `bin/fox` (+ sidecar `libopentui.so`) · npm `fox-agent`\n\n---\n\n## Identity\n- Name: `foxc` → renamed **fox-agent** (npm blocked \"foxc\" as too similar to solc; CLI is `fox`).\n- Avoided trademark traps: qodex (~Codex), foxcode/openfox (taken), clawd-style near-misses.\n\n## Locked design decisions (do not reopen)\n\n| Area | Decision |\n|---|---|\n| Language | TypeScript on Bun (one language core→TUI→plugins→future web) |\n| Core | ~80-line agent loop; everything else = tools/hooks |\n| Core tools | read/write/edit/glob/grep/exec/ctx — the harness itself |\n| Bundled-plugin tools | pty, todo, fetch, repl, **task**, question, lsp, cost, mcp — ship as plugins so they can be shadowed or `disabledPlugins`-ed |\n| Context | inline `[mN]` markers on every message; NO history_list tool — LLM sees IDs natively |\n| ctx_edit | batched delete(+summary placeholder)/replace ops; view-only, storage immutable |\n| Sessions | SQLite WAL, INSERT-only message DAG (`parent_id`), `refs` table (branches/reverts), `ops` table (view surgery events) |\n| Permissions | NONE — pi-style full control; env passthrough |\n| Providers | thin Provider port; bundled openai-compatible / openai-responses / anthropic / google plugins |\n| UI | wrapper-first TUI on @opentui/solid (rejected linear-stream: needs owned viewport for history rewrite) |\n\n### Plugin trust boundary (do not reopen)\n**Plugins load from the GLOBAL config only.** A `plugins` key in a project `fox-agent.toml` is ignored with a warning. Reason: every other extension point (`[mcpServers.*]`, `[agents.*]`, `[lsp.*]`) spawns a child through `childEnv()` which strips secrets; a plugin is imported into fox's own process and inherits the whole environment, API key included. So \"clone a repo, cd in, run fox\" must not execute that repo's code.\n\n**Hooks are patch-based and additive.** `beforeLLMCall` returns `{appendSystem?}`, `afterTool` returns `{output?}`. Neither can reorder/drop messages, so `renderContext`'s invariant (every assistant `tool_call` followed by its `tool_result`) holds by construction.\n\n### Provider token accounting (researched, verified)\n`StreamEvent.usage` = `{ prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cached_tokens? }`, normalized by the AI SDK so **`prompt_tokens` is the billed TOTAL and `cached_tokens` is the subset read from cache — never sum them.**\n- **OpenAI Chat Completions**: `prompt_tokens` total incl. cached; `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` subset; `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` (o1+).\n- **Anthropic**: `input_tokens` total, `cache_read_input_tokens` (read, cheap), `cache_creation_input_tokens` (WRITTEN this call, the premium).\n- **Google Gemini**: `promptTokenCount`, `cachedContentTokenCount`, `candidatesTokenCount`.\n\n**kimi-for-coding under-reports**: it tokenizes loosely, `prompt_tokens` ≈ 1/word (~25% under chars/4). [974]agent

The leftover-bottom-bar fix is done and pushed (0dd46a7).

 

The bug

 

gracefulExit called term.end() to leave the alt screen, but never cancelled the pending paintTimer. The timer is unref'd so it never blocked process exit — but if it fired in the window between the last paint and the process actually exiting, the frame loop ran paintStatus() and wrote the status bar to the primary screen (the alt screen was already gone). That's the bar you saw lingering after quit.

 

The fix

 

• Gate the scheduled tick on the exiting flag — a frame queued before exit won't paint once teardown starts.

• Cancel the pending paintTimer directly in gracefulExit, so nothing can paint between term.end() and process exit.

 

Built clean, 25 TUI tests pass, tsc clean.

 

This was a race, so it would have been intermittent — which matches "sometimes." If you still catch it happening after this build, tell me and I'll dig further (there's a second, less likely path: a synchronous paint mid-teardown).

1: /**

2: * Incremental row production for streaming text — the kernel that turns

3: * "text grew by a delta" into "here is the repaint window".

4: *

5: * Region model:

6: * - SETTLED: everything up to the last newline. Rendered exactly once

7: * (the old cut loop, verbatim — fence state carried forward), appended

8: * immutably. Cost: only the newly settled region.

9: * - TAIL: the unterminated chunk after it. Re-parsed and re-wrapped per

10: * feed today (identical to the previous renderer's tail behavior —

11: * byte-identical output is the contract); the wrap-reuse optimization

12: * lands on top once the golden test pins equivalence.

13: *

14: * The previous renderer's headline cost was re-parsing AND re-wrapping the

15: * whole tail per frame at 30fps. The parse is the same here — the win this

16: * commit ships is architectural: a per-feed repaint window (from), so the

17: * CALLER stops re-stamping everything, and a single testable kernel that the

18: * wrap reuse attaches to next. Output is byte-identical to the old path

19: * (legacyStreamRows kept for the golden test), quirks included: the

20: * paragraph-straddle line split, and the empty-tail caret row.

21: */

22: import { renderMarkdown, type MdState } from "./markdown.ts";

23: import { wrapSegs, type Seg } from "./wrap.ts";

24:

25: /** One painted row: styled segments. Same shape layout.ts stamps with. */

26: export interface Row {

27: segs: Seg[];

28: }

29:

30: /** The old renderer, verbatim, for the golden equivalence test. */

31: export function legacyStreamRows(

32: text: string,

33: w: number,

34: cache?: { cut: number; md: MdState; prefix: Row[]; text: string },

35: ): Row[] {

36: const c = cache ?? { cut: 0, md: { inFence: false, hadCode: false }, prefix: [], text: "" };

37: if (!text.startsWith(c.text.slice(0, c.cut))) {

38: c.cut = 0;

39: c.md = { inFence: false, hadCode: false };

40: c.prefix = [];

41: c.text = "";

42: }

43: let scan = c.cut;

44: let newCut = c.cut;

45: const md2 = { ...c.md };

46: for (;;) {

47: const nl = text.indexOf("\n", scan);

48: if (nl < 0) break;

49: if (/^```/.test(text.slice(scan, nl))) {

50: md2.inFence = !md2.inFence;

51: md2.hadCode = false;

52: } else if (md2.inFence) {

53: md2.hadCode = true;

54: }

55: newCut = nl + 1;

56: scan = nl + 1;

57: }

58: if (newCut > c.cut) {

59: for (const mline of renderMarkdown(text.slice(c.cut, newCut - 1), c.md, w)) {

60: c.prefix.push(...wrapSegs(mline, w).map((segs) => ({ segs })));

61: }

62: c.cut = newCut;

63: c.md = md2;

64: }

65: c.text = text;

66: const rows = c.prefix.slice();

67: for (const mline of renderMarkdown(text.slice(c.cut), { ...c.md }, w)) {

68: rows.push(...wrapSegs(mline, w).map((segs) => ({ segs })));

69: }

70: return rows;

71: }

72:

73: export interface StreamRows {

74: /** all rows so far — treat as immutable; callers never mutate */

75: readonly rows: readonly Row[];

76: /**

77: * Feed more text. Returns the index in rows where repainting must

78: * start: rows before it are untouched since the previous call.

79: */

80: feed(delta: string): { from: number };

81: /** Width change: reflows everything; rows is rebuilt in full. */

82: resize(w: number): void;

83: }

84:

85: /** Index of the seg containing character offset pos of the concatenated

86: * seg text; segs.length when pos is at/after the end. */

87: function segIndexOf(segs: Seg[], pos: number): number {

88: let acc = 0;

89: for (let i = 0; i < segs.length; i++) {

90: acc += segs[i].t.length;

91: if (pos < acc) return i;

92: }

93: return segs.length;

94: }

96: export function createStreamRows(w: number): StreamRows {

97: let width = w;

98: let text = "";

99: let settledRows: Row[] = [];

100: let settledCut = 0;

101: let md: MdState = { inFence: false, hadCode: false };

102: /** the tail's wrapped visual lines (the tail region of rows) */

103: let tailLines: Seg[][] = [];

104: /** the parsed segments tailLines was wrapped from */

105: let tailSegs: Seg[] = [];

106: /** char offset (in concatenated tail seg text) at which each of the

107: * current tailLines ENDS — the reuse boundaries */

108: let tailCharEnds: number[] = [];

109: /** the markdown state the current tailLines were rendered under */

110: let tailMd: MdState = { inFence: false, hadCode: false };

111:

112: /** Settle everything up to the last newline (the old cut loop, verbatim). */

113: const settle = (): boolean => {

async function copyText(text: string) {

if (!text) return;

const okd = await clipWrite(text, term);

const lines = text.split("\n").length;

flash(okd ? copied ${text.length} chars${lines > 1 ? (${lines} lines) : ""} : "copy failed — no clipboard tool");

}

 

/** Everything waiting to send, oldest first, as dock rows.

*

* Queued next-turn messages, then steers parked for the running turn's next

* step boundary. Both stay painted above the input until they are actually

* sent: a queued row vanishes when drainQueue dispatches it, a steering row

* when the turn's drainSteer consumes it — the same moment its steered

* event lands in the transcript. One helper for paint() and onClick() so the

* hit-test can never disagree with the pixels about how many rows these are.

*/

function pendingLines(): string[] {

const lines = queued.map((q, i) => queued ${i + 1}/${queued.length}: ${oneLine(q.raw)});

const steers = state.sessionId ? peekSteer(state.sessionId) : [];

steers.forEach((s, i) => lines.push(steering ${i + 1}/${steers.length}: ${oneLine(s)}));

return lines;

}

 

function oneLine(s: string): string {

return s.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim() || "(whitespace)";

}

I've now read all the core infrastructure. Let me design this carefully before touching code, since it has a release gate.

 

The core problem

 

The [N] marker is currently baked into the text — [${m.seq}] ❯ ${m.content} — injected only in selectHistory (the settled projection). The live path (runAgent) pushes ❯ ${raw} with no marker, and the streaming text (streamText) / streaming tool pairs / think blocks have no seq until they settle. So a marker "appears" only after refresh rebuilds items from history.

 

The user wants markers as a rendered gutter column with a distinct background, present from the moment a message exists (including in-flight), clickable, opening an ops wizard (fork/copy/revert).

 

The design

 

The cleanest approach that satisfies "as fast as possible" (markers on live content immediately) without rewriting the whole row pipeline:

 

1. Add a seq field to Item, separate from text.

- Stop baking [N] into it.text. Instead it.seq holds the storage seq.

- selectHistory sets it.seq = m.seq (and removes the [N] prefix from text).

- The live path: when runAgent sends the user message, we don't have a seq yet (it's assigned on append). But we can capture it — appendMessage returns the row with seq. Actually the turn loop appends. Let me check if runTurn/appendMessage surfaces the user seq... For the user message specifically, I can append it synchronously in runAgent before streaming and capture the seq.

 

2. Render the marker as a leading gutter column in itemRows.

- For items with it.seq !== undefined, prepend a marker cell: [N] with a distinct bg (a new theme slot, e.g. C.markerBg), at the start of the first row of the item; continuation rows indent by the marker width.

- This is the tricky part for wrapped content: the marker occupies columns 0..k on the first row only, and the text wraps in the remaining width. The row pipeline wraps at width w — I'd wrap text at w - markerWidth and prepend the marker seg to the first row, spaces to continuation rows.

 

3. Marker hit-area for clicks.

- In onClick, before the code-block/toggle logic, check if the click x falls within the marker column (0..markerWidth) of a row owned by an item with a seq → open the ops wizard for that seq.

 

4. Ops wizard.

- Reuse askPrompt with a select step: options fork / copy / revert, then dispatch:

- fork: forkSession(sessionId, seq) (cut at marker).

- copy: copy the message content to clipboard.

- revert: this is the hard one — "revert" at a message means roll the session back to just before that message. There's no existing primitive. /undo uses undoLastOp (view ops). The closest is forkSession(uptoSeq = seq-1) then switch to the fork... but that creates a new session rather than reverting in place. Actually "revert" here most likely means: hide/truncate everything after this marker. Let me check what prune.ts offers.

 

Let me read prune.ts and check whether there's a truncate-in-place primitive before I commit to the revert design.

1: /**

2: * Reclaim disk from context that is already invisible.

3: *

4: * Auto-compaction only hides messages: it appends a delete op and the bodies

5: * stay in the log so /undo can bring them back. Over a long session that is

6: * most of the file. Prune makes the hiding physical.

7: *

8: * The subtlety that makes this more than a DELETE: a compaction's summary is

9: * stored on the op, but renderContext only emits it while the *first message

10: * row of the hidden span* still exists (it hangs the "(ctx: [N] summarized

11: * away)" line off that node). Deleting every hidden row therefore drops the

12: * summary from the prompt and silently loses the context the compaction was

13: * meant to preserve. So each summarized span keeps its anchor row as an empty

14: * stub, and only the bodies go.

15: */

16: import { sessionDb, rid } from "./db.ts";

17: import { projectView, dropViewCache } from "../context/view.ts";

18: import { dropRenderCache } from "../context/render.ts";

19: import type { DeleteOp, ViewOp } from "./db.ts";

20: import { allOps } from "./db.ts";

21:

22: export interface PruneReport {

23: /** rows whose body would be / was removed */

24: messages: number;

25: /** anchor rows blanked but kept so their summary still renders */

26: stubs: number;

27: /** orphaned usage rows removed */

28: usage: number;

29: bytesBefore: number;

30: bytesAfter: number;

31: /** false when nothing was written (dry run, or nothing to do) */

32: applied: boolean;

33: /** compact mode: summary rows spliced in, remaining seqs renumbered 1..n */

34: compacted?: { summaries: number; renumbered: number };

35: }

36:

37: function dbBytes(sessionId: string): number {

38: const d = sessionDb(sessionId);

39: const p = d.query("PRAGMA pagecount").get() as { pagecount: number };

40: const s = d.query("PRAGMA pagesize").get() as { pagesize: number };

41: return p.pagecount * s.pagesize;

42: }

43:

44: /**

45: * Seqs that must survive as stubs: the anchor of every summarized delete span.

46: *

47: * Mirrors projectView's rule — the summary lands on the first node of the span

48: * that was not already hidden — so the anchor computed here is the same row the

49: * renderer will look for.

50: */

51: function summaryAnchors(sessionId: string): Set<number> {

52: const anchors = new Set<number>();

53: const hidden = new Set<number>();

54: for (const row of allOps(sessionId)) {

55: let op: ViewOp;

56: try {

57: op = JSON.parse(row.payload) as ViewOp;

58: } catch {

59: continue;

60: }

61: if (op.kind === "restore") {

62: for (const id of op.ids) hidden.delete(id);

63: continue;

64: }

65: if (op.kind !== "delete") continue;

66: const del = op as DeleteOp;

67: let first = true;

68: for (const id of del.ids) {

69: if (hidden.has(id)) continue;

70: hidden.add(id);

71: if (del.summary && first) {

72: anchors.add(id);

73: first = false;

74: }

75: }

76: }

77: return anchors;

78: }

79:

80: /**

81: * Summarized spans, in anchor order: what compact mode turns into real rows.

82: * Walks the op log exactly like summaryAnchors but keeps the summary text.

83: */

84: function summarySpans(sessionId: string): { anchor: number; summary: string }[] {

85: const out: { anchor: number; summary: string }[] = [];

86: const hidden = new Set<number>();

87: for (const row of allOps(sessionId)) {

88: let op: ViewOp;

89: try {

90: op = JSON.parse(row.payload) as ViewOp;

91: } catch {

92: continue;

93: }

94: if (op.kind === "restore") {

95: for (const id of op.ids) hidden.delete(id);

96: continue;

97: }

98: if (op.kind !== "delete") continue;

99: const del = op as DeleteOp;

100: let first = true;

101: for (const id of del.ids) {

102: if (hidden.has(id)) continue;

103: hidden.add(id);

104: if (del.summary && first) {

105: out.push({ anchor: id, summary: del.summary });

106: first = false;

107: }

108: }

109: }

110: return out.sort((a, b) => a.anchor - b.anchor);

111: }

112:

113: /**

114: * Physically remove hidden message bodies. One-way: pruned text cannot be

115: * restored by /undo afterward, though the op log itself is left intact so

116: * projection still replays correctly.

117: *

118: * mode: "compact" goes further: the summary anchors are deleted too, each

119: * span's summary is spliced back in as a REAL assistant row at the span's old

120: * position, the op log is cleared (projection of the surviving rows is then

121: * trivially "all visible" — remapping stale op seqs onto renumbered rows could

122: * otherwise un-delete the WRONG row), and the remaining seqs are renumbered to

123: * a contiguous 1..n so transcript markers carry no gaps. Even more one-way

124: * than the default mode: /undo history goes with the op log.

125: */

126: export function pruneSession(

127: sessionId: string,

128: opts: { dryRun?: boolean; mode?: "default" | "compact" } = {},

129: ): PruneReport {

130: const d = sessionDb(sessionId);

131: const view = projectView(sessionId);

132: const compact = opts.mode === "compact";

133: const anchors = compact ? new Set<number>() : summaryAnchors(sessionId);

134:

135: // An orphan is hidden only as a consequence of its assistant being hidden

136: // (pairing repair), not by an op. Pruning it is still correct — it cannot

137: // become visible again while its assistant is gone — but it has no body worth

138: // keeping either way, so it is treated like any other hidden row.

146:

147: const bytesBefore = dbBytes(sessionId);

150: messages: toDelete.length,

151: stubs: toStub.length,

152: usage: countOrphanUsage(sessionId, toDelete),

153: bytesBefore,

154: bytesAfter: bytesBefore,

155: applied: false,

156: };

157: }
