1: // styled text segments + width-aware word wrapping

2: import { charWidth } from "./screen.ts";

3:

4: export interface Seg {

5: t: string;

6: fg?: string;

7: bg?: string;

8: bold?: boolean;

9: italic?: boolean;

10: /** strikethrough (text) — SGR 9/29 at flush time */

11: strike?: boolean;

12: /** hyperlink target: rendered as an OSC 8 hyperlink, never printed as text */

13: href?: string;

14: }

15:

16: export function segWidth(s: string): number {

17: return Bun.stringWidth(s);

18: }

19:

20: /**

21: * Wrap segs to visual lines (greedy, width-aware).

22: *

23: * rawEnds (optional) records, per output line, how many INPUT segs were

24: * fully consumed by the time the line ENDED — a line may START mid-seg

25: * (long segs split across lines), so a line's raw range is

26: * [prevEnd, rawEnds[i]) in input-seg units plus possibly a prefix of

27: * rawSegs[prevEnd]. Callers using ranges for incremental re-wrap must only

28: * reuse lines whose range ENDS at a raw boundary (rawEnds[i] > rawEnds[i-1]

29: * means this line finished a seg; ending mid-seg is fine as long as the

30: * NEXT line starts at the same raw index — see rows.ts).

31: */

32: export function wrapSegs(segs: Seg[], width: number, rawEnds?: number[], opts?: { keepLeadSpaces?: boolean }): Seg[][] {

33: if (width < 4) width = 4;

34: // per-line callers (the think kernel wraps one source line at a time) must

35: // see the same rule a whole-text wrap applies to every line AFTER the first:

36: // leading spaces are kept. Whole-text wraps keep the default — spaces at the

37: // very start of the output are layout noise and stay suppressed.

38: const leadKept = !!opts?.keepLeadSpaces;

39: const out: Seg[][] = [];

40: let line: Seg[] = [];

41: let lineW = 0;

42: let rawIdx = 0; // input segs fully consumed so far

43: let lastRawEnd = 0; // raw segs consumed by PREVIOUS completed lines

44:

45: const push = (seg: Seg) => {

46: line.push(seg);

47: lineW += segWidth(seg.t);

48: };

49: const newline = () => {

50: out.push(line);

51: if (rawEnds) rawEnds.push(rawIdx);

52: lastRawEnd = rawIdx;

53: line = [];

54: lineW = 0;

55: };

56:

57: for (const raw of segs) {

58: const parts = raw.t.split(/(\n| +)/);

59: for (const part of parts) {

60: if (!part) continue;

61: if (part === "\n") {

62: newline();

63: continue;

64: }

65: if (/^ +$/.test(part)) {

66: const room = width - 1 - lineW;

67: const sp = Math.min(part.length, Math.max(0, room));

68: if (sp > 0 && (leadKept || line.length > 0 || out.length > 0)) {

69: push({ ...raw, t: " ".repeat(sp) });

70: }

71: continue;

72: }

73: let word = part;

74: for (;;) {

75: const ww = segWidth(word);

76: if (lineW + ww <= width - 1) {

77: push({ ...raw, t: word });

78: break;

79: }

80: if (line.length === 0) {

81: // lone oversized word: fill the line then continue

82: let take = "";

83: let tw = 0;

84: for (const ch of word) {

85: const cw = charWidth(ch.codePointAt(0)!);

86: if (tw + cw > width - 1) break;

87: take += ch;

88: tw += cw;

89: }

90: if (!take) break;

91: push({ ...raw, t: take });

92: newline();

93: word = word.slice(take.length);

94: if (!word) break;

95: continue;

96: }

97: newline();

98: }

99: }

100: rawIdx++; // this input seg is fully distributed (possibly across lines)

101: }

102: if (line.length || !out.length) {

103: out.push(line);

104: if (rawEnds) rawEnds.push(rawIdx);

105: }

106: return out;

107: }

1: /**

2: * TUI themes. One palette type covers both the app and the standalone picker

3: * (fox -c); presets plus whatever plugins register (FoxPlugin.themes).

4: *

5: * The current theme is module-level and mutable so /theme can switch live

6: * without a restart: both consumers hold a proxy that resolves every property

7: * access against the active palette.

8: *

9: * Contrast contract: chrome/hint render the workhorse secondary text

10: * (hints, the slash list, queued rows, tool bodies) and must hold >= 4.5:1

11: * against BOTH barBg and inputBg; fg >= 4.5 against inputBg. The

12: * first palettes shipped prettier-but-illegible grays (default's chrome

13: * measured 2.5:1, light's 1.8:1) — keep new palettes honest.

14: */

15:

18: user: string;

20: info: string;

21: hint: string;

22: error: string;

23: chrome: string;

25: accent: string;

30: * generic accent (spinner, slash-list headers, flash messages).

31: */

32: prompt?: string;

33: /**

36: * command text stays inputFg.

45: inputBg: string;

46: selBg: string;

47: /** background under tool-call rows (heads + bodies), subtly different from inputBg */

48: toolBg: string;

49: /** thinking/reasoning blocks — a distinct cool tone, not the tool amber */

50: think: string;

51: /**

52: * Floating command-output panels (/todo, /usage, /help boxes) — optional,

53: * falls back to inputBg so every theme gets a visible panel without edits.

54: * Unfilled, those boxes sat on the terminal's own background, which reads

55: * as a plain black slab unrelated to the theme.

56: */

57: panelBg?: string;

309: let current: Theme = THEME_PRESETS.default;

310: let currentName = "default";

311: const extra = new Map<string, Theme>();

312:

313: /** Plugin-registered themes, available alongside the presets. */

314: export function registerThemes(themes: Record<string, Theme>): void {

315: for (const [name, t] of Object.entries(themes)) {

316: if (name in THEME_PRESETS) continue; // a plugin may not repaint a preset

317: extra.set(name, t);

318: }

319: }

320:

321: export function themeNames(): string[] {

322: return [...Object.keys(THEME_PRESETS), ...extra.keys()];

323: }

324:

325: export function theme(): Theme {

326: return current;

327: }

328: export function themeName(): string {

329: return currentName;

330: }

331:

332: /** Switch by name; false when the name is unknown (the caller reports it). */

333: export function setTheme(name: string): boolean {

334: const t = THEME_PRESETS[name] ?? extra.get(name);

335: if (!t) return false;

336: current = t;

337: currentName = name;

338: return true;

339: }

340:

341: /**

342: * A live view of the active theme: every property get resolves against whatever

343: * theme is current now, so a /theme switch repaints without a restart.

344: */

345: export function liveTheme<T extends string>(map?: Partial<Record<T, keyof Theme>>): Record<T, string> {

346: return new Proxy({} as Record<T, string>, {

347: get: (_, key: T) => {

348: const k = (map?.[key] ?? key) as keyof Theme;

349: return current[k];

350: },

351: });

352: }

{"edits":[{"newString":"  /**\n   * Prepend the leading [N] gutter marker to an item's rows. 258:export function itemEdgeSpan(rows: readonly Row[]): [number, number] {

export function itemEdgeSpan(rows: readonly Row[]): [number, number] {

let a = 0;

let b = rows.length;

while (a < b && !rows[a].segs.length) a++;

while (b > a && !rows[b - 1].segs.length) b--;

return [a, b];

}

 

/** Scrollbar geometry for rows lines in a viewport of vh. */

export interface ScrollbarGeom {

showing: boolean;

ty: number;

th: number;

}

export function scrollbarGeom(rows: number, vh: number, scrollTop: number): ScrollbarGeom {

if (rows <= vh || vh < 4) return { showing: false, ty: 0, th: vh };

const th = Math.max(1, Math.floor((vh * vh) / rows));

const maxScroll = rows - vh;

const ty = maxScroll > 0 ? Math.floor((Math.max(0, Math.min(scrollTop, maxScroll)) / maxScroll) * (vh - th)) : 0;

return { showing: true, ty, th };

}

//

// The assertions live in scripts/acp-accept.ts, not here. That check needs a

// nature; this wrapper exists so bun test runs it when the pieces are present

// instead of leaving it to be remembered by hand.

//

// Doubly gated, and neither gate is incidental:

// - acpx is an optional global install, so a contributor without it must not

// see a failure (the test/pty.test.ts:12 pattern).

// - bin/fox-agent is a build artifact. Gating on it rather than building here keeps

// bun test from silently taking a minute-long detour through the bundler,

// and keeps this from passing against a stale binary without saying so.

import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";

import { existsSync } from "node:fs";

import { join } from "node:path";

 

const ROOT = join(import.meta.dir, "..");

const FOX = join(ROOT, "bin", "fox");

const SCRIPT = join(ROOT, "scripts", "acp-accept.ts");

 

const HAS_ACPX = Bun.which("acpx") !== null;

const HAS_BIN = existsSync(FOX);

const CANRUN = HASACPX && HAS_BIN;

 

if (!CAN_RUN) {

console.log(acp.live: skipped (${!HAS_ACPX ? "acpx not on PATH" : "bin/fox not built — run bun run build"}));

}

test("acpx drives the built binary end to end", async () => {

const [out, err, code] = await Promise.all([new Response(p.stdout).text(), new Response(p.stderr).text(), p.exited]);

The pieces:

- Item gained a seq field; loadItems sets it and no longer bakes [N] into text. itemRows renders the marker as a leading gutter chip (new markerBg theme slot, falls back to selBg), indenting continuation rows so wrapped text stays aligned under the content.

- A new user AgentEvent surfaces the user message's seq the instant runTurnCore persists it, so the just-sent line shows its marker in-flight — this was the actual gap you reported.

- Clicking a marker opens an ops wizard: fork (cut the session at [N], /fork semantics), copy (message body to clipboard), or revert (hide [N] and everything after from the context window via a ctx delete op — reversible with /undo, storage stays append-only).

// (and a cell the new frame does NOT write is transparent, revealing

// the grid's last composite — which is exactly what stale-ghosting

// used to require clearRows choreography to avoid)

P.transcript.clearRows(0, H);

 

// fr.rows is the WINDOW built around scrollTop (total is the real

// length): rows[0] is absolute row fr.scrollTop - fr.winOffset, and the

// viewport starts winOffset rows INTO the slice — rows before it are

// scroll-up margin, never on screen

const winBase = fr.scrollTop - fr.winOffset;

let y = 0;

for (let i = fr.winOffset; i < fr.rowCount && y < fr.vh; i++, y++) {

const row = fr.rows[i];

const absolute = winBase + i;

// tool rows fill the background first, so the text paints over it

// instead of floating in default. NEVER the last column — that cell

// belongs to the scrollbar strip (the strip's track/thumb must show

// through even on tool rows)

if (row.bg) P.transcript.fillRow(y, 0, SCROLLBAR ? W - 1 : W, row.bg);

let x = 1;

for (const seg of row.segs) {

x = P.transcript.text(x, y, seg.t, st(seg, S.base));

}

// Selection is a re-style over the cells already painted, not a second

// text pass: one char per cell, so re-stamping the range with a

// highlight background cannot disturb wide chars or wrapping.

if (hasSel()) {

const range = selRangeForRow(absolute, selA!, selB!, rowCells(row.segs));

if (range) P.transcript.restyle(y, 1 + range.from, 2 + range.to, C.selBg);

}

}

=== build.ts ===

// fox-agent build: single-binary compile straight from source (no dist intermediates).

// Uses process.execPath so it works regardless of how bun is on PATH.

// --bytecode caches compiled JS bytecode in the binary (measured: TTFF ~2x

// faster, ~6MB less idle PSS); --minify is a small extra win on top.

const proc = Bun.spawnSync(

[process.execPath, "build", "--compile", "--bytecode", "--minify", "./src/cli.ts", "--outfile", "./bin/fox"],

{ stdout: "inherit", stderr: "inherit" },

);

process.exit(proc.exitCode);

The user asked two questions I can answer with data I now have. Let me explain the bundle size and the app.ts split.

 

Bundle size (115MB): The build uses bun build --compile (build.ts), which embeds the entire Bun runtime as a statically-linked ELF binary. That's the dominant cost — the Bun runtime + bytecode cache is ~100MB+ on its own. The shiki highlighter adds only ~14MB of grammars (in node_modules/@shikijs), a small slice. So the answer: it's mostly Bun's embedded runtime, NOT your source or the highlighter. It was "smaller before" likely because earlier you ran via bun src/cli.ts (JIT, no embedded runtime) or an older Bun runtime was leaner.
